items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Severe acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with heterogeneous outcomes, whereas conventional risk assessment focuses largely on neurological deficits and imaging-defined injury, with limited consideration of systemic metabolic status. The cholesterol–high-density lipoprotein–glucose (CHG) index integrates markers of glucose and lipid metabolism and may capture this additional risk dimension.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This retrospective single-center study included 536 patients with severe anterior-circulation AIS admitted between May 2023 and May 2026. CHG was calculated from fasting plasma glucose (FPG), total cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. The primary outcome was the full 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) distribution; the secondary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality. Associations were assessed using ordinal logistic and Cox regression, with sensitivity analyses addressing model assumptions. Binary prediction models for poor functional outcome (mRS 3–6) and mortality included age, sex, admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, and baseline Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score, with and without CHG. Component comparisons and a Full clinical reference model were also examined. Performance assessment included discrimination, calibration, Brier scores, decision-curve analysis, and 1,000-resample bootstrap internal validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Poor functional outcome occurred in 420 patients (78.4%), and 118 (22.0%) died within 28 days. In adjusted analyses, each standard deviation increase in CHG was associated with worse mRS (common odds ratio, 2.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.34–3.38) and mortality (hazard ratio, 2.28; 95% CI, 1.90–2.74). Time-varying analyses suggested a stronger mortality association later in follow-up. Adding CHG increased the apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.755 to 0.828 for poor functional outcome (ΔAUC, 0.073; 95% CI, 0.039–0.107) and from 0.728 to 0.826 for mortality (ΔAUC, 0.098; 95% CI, 0.055–0.142). Optimism-corrected Brier scores were lower after adding CHG, corrected calibration-in-the-large and calibration slopes were close to their ideal values, and decision curves suggested potential net benefit at selected thresholds. Apparent discrimination gains over FPG were small and uncertain.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CHG was associated with adverse outcomes and added predictive information to clinical–imaging models. Its predictive advantage over FPG remained uncertain. Prospective external validation and assessment of clinical usefulness are needed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Incremental prognostic value of the cholesterol–high-density lipoprotein–glucose index in severe anterior-circulation acute ischemic stroke

items.abstract: <jats:p>A spatial beam-combining and fiber-coupling architecture for double-ridge semiconductor lasers is numerically investigated using a 638 nm source. Long-focal-length slow-axis collimation reduces angular separation, and a common dual-wedge unit improves focal-spot overlap after focusing. A circular-aperture packing model guides two mirror stages for beam rearrangement. The feasible 46-channel layout accommodates 39.39% more beams than a 33-channel rectangular reference. Polarization combining of two modules gives a simulated coupled output of 241.5 W at 87.5% optical-to-optical efficiency, approximately 130% above the single-ridge comparison at the same device count and assumed efficiency. Tolerance analysis further highlights the importance of controlling mirror angular errors for efficient fiber coupling.</jats:p>
title: High-density multi-chip spatial beam combining and fiber coupling system for 638  nm double-ridge semiconductor lasers

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      <jats:italic>Phytophthora</jats:italic>
                      is a destructive soilborne pathogen causing citrus tree decline, yield losses, and reduced orchard productivity worldwide. Developing resistant rootstocks is the most sustainable strategy for long-term disease management.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      With the objective of mapping the
                      <jats:italic>Phytophthora</jats:italic>
                      resistance, a high-density SNP-based linkage map was developed using F
                      <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                      population comprising 144 hybrids, obtained from cross of susceptible parent ‘Rough lemon’ and resistant parent ‘Swingle citrumelo’. The constructed linkage map consisted of 2,195 high-quality unilocus SNP markers assigned to nine linkage groups, covering 1,438.7 cM with an average marker spacing of 0.7 cM. Phenotyping was conducted using an integrated disease severity scale based on feeder root rot, gummosis and chlorosis symptoms to ensure comprehensive and reliable assessment of
                      <jats:italic>Phytophthora</jats:italic>
                      resistance along with bark cracking as an independent trait for three years.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results and discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Quantitative Trait Locus (QTL) analysis identified total five QTLs associated with disease resistance across two chromosomes (8 and 9), explaining 7.53-12.62% phenotypic variation. Candidate gene analysis within the identified co-localised QTL
                      <jats:italic>(qPDR_8.1</jats:italic>
                      ) revealed genes involved in diverse defense-related pathways, including pathogen perception, signal transduction, transcriptional regulation, protein turnover, secondary metabolism, stress adaptation and cell wall modification. The functional assessment of these putative candidate genes supports the polygenic and multifaceted nature of quantitative disease resistance. This study provides a comprehensive multi-trait and multi-year QTL analysis of
                      <jats:italic>Phytophthora</jats:italic>
                      disease resistance in citrus and establishes a valuable genomic resource for fine-mapping and marker-assisted breeding aimed at developing durable
                      <jats:italic>Phytophthora</jats:italic>
                      -resistant citrus rootstocks.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: QTL mapping of Phytophthora resistance in citrus using high-density SNP-based linkage map

items.abstract: <jats:p>This article introduces three proposed topologies, each an extension of the conventional DC-DC positive output super lift Luo converter (POSLLC). By incorporating a switched-inductor (SL) cell into the POSLLC, the three modified POSLLC topologies succeed to provide a high output voltage along with a significant voltage gain. A high-voltage gain DC-DC converter is a crucial element in renewable energy systems, particularly in photovoltaic (PV) applications. It boosts the voltage before the converter is connected to a DC load or an AC load through an inverter, since the output voltage from a PV module is relatively low. The proposed designs provide several favorable features, including the utilization of only one controlled switch, continuous input current, the availability of common ground between the input and output, and the generation of a positive output voltage polarity. The proposed three topologies can provide a voltage gain of 8, 14, and 15, in comparison with only 5 in the original POSLLC when the duty cycle is 75%. MATLAB/Simulink models were developed and simulated to evaluate the consistency of the theoretical results obtained.</jats:p>
title: Three Topologies of Transformer-less High-Gain Step-up Luo Converter for Renewable Energy Applications

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The
                    <jats:italic>Vision of Dorotheus</jats:italic>
                    (P.Bodmer 29; =
                    <jats:italic>VD</jats:italic>
                    ), part of the “Codex of Visions” (P.Bodmer 29–38), narrates the visionary experiences of a fourth-century Christian named Dorotheus, who is portrayed as a doorkeeper at the gates of God’s heavenly imperial palace. Much of the scholarly focus on
                    <jats:italic>VD</jats:italic>
                    in recent decades has been on how the late ancient Christian author of the text deployed Homeric epic to tell a Christian story, as well as how we might glean social-historical data from its depiction of late Roman military imagery. In this article, I propose another angle by which
                    <jats:italic>VD</jats:italic>
                    might be fruitfully analyzed: slavery studies. I argue that Dorotheus’s status as a doorkeeper mirrors Roman literary stereotypes about the labor of enslaved persons who were forced to guard enslaver’s doors and gates, and well provides insight into how a late ancient Christian author characterized the role of enslavement within God’s divine household. Despite attempting to flee his post at God’s door, Dorotheus in
                    <jats:italic>VD</jats:italic>
                    ends up functioning as a literary model for late ancient Christian readers to emulate in their own social-theological statuses as God’s enslaved persons (δοῦλοι).
                  </jats:p>
title: Dorotheus the Doorkeeper: Slavery and Confinement in the Vision of Dorotheus

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Ultrathin Cu(In,Ga)Se
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    (CIGS) solar cells offer a promising route to reducing material consumption while maintaining the advantages of high-efficiency thin-film photovoltaics. However, reducing the absorber thickness leads to incomplete light absorption and limits device performance. Here, we develop a reflective back contact architecture to enhance light trapping in a 600 nm-thick CIGS absorber. Device performance was further improved by tailoring the CIGS deposition process and applying a 15 min RbF post-deposition treatment, leading to enhanced optoelectronic properties. The resulting devices reach a power conversion efficiency of 15.8%, which,demonstrating competitive performance among previously reported ultrathin CIGS solar cells with comparable absorber thicknesses. These results demonstrate a pathway to high-efficiency ultrathin CIGS solar cells through the combination of optical engineering, alkali treatment, and absorber growth control.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Synergistic reflective back contact and absorber engineering for high-efficiency ultrathin Cu(In,Ga)Se
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    solar cells

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Inverted V‐shaped high tibial osteotomy (iV‐HTO) is used for advanced medial knee osteoarthritis with severe varus deformity or concomitant patellofemoral (PF) osteoarthritis. However, its effects on in vivo knee loading remain unclear. This study evaluated changes in femorotibial (FT) and PF subchondral bone density distributions after iV‐HTO using computed tomography (CT)‐osteoabsorptiometry. This retrospective study included 21 patients (23 knees) who underwent iV‐HTO with preoperative and postoperative CT scans. High‐density areas (HDAs) on the proximal tibia, femoral trochlea, and patella were defined as regions with the highest 20% of Hounsfield unit values. Medial ratios (the proportion of medial compartment HDA to total HDA) and regional HDA percentages (%HDA) were compared between the time points. The FT medial ratio significantly decreased by 9.2% after iV‐HTO (
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     < 0.001). The %HDA significantly decreased in the central medial tibial region (M2) and increased in the medial regions of the lateral compartment (L1 and L2) (all adjusted
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     ≤ 0.001). Trochlear %HDA significantly increased medially and decreased laterally, whereas patellar %HDA increased at the central ridge and decreased in the lateral portion of the lateral facet (all adjusted
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     ≤ 0.033). IV‐HTO produced distinct FT and PF subchondral bone density redistribution patterns, suggesting altered cumulative loading in both joints.
                  </jats:p>
title: Inverted V‐Shaped High Tibial Osteotomy Alters Subchondral Bone Density Distribution in the Femorotibial and Patellofemoral Joints in Medial Knee Osteoarthritis

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Achieving long-term durability without sacrificing performance is a critical challenge for solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs). Here, we introduce a high-entropy perovskite oxide (HEPO) design strategy, demonstrating a HEPO (La0.2Sr0.2Ca0.2Nd0.2Y0.2)(Co0.2Fe0.8)O3–δ (CaNdY), with great chemical stability and high electrochemical activity. CaNdY was synthesized via an optimized solution combustion method, and the resulting dual-phase perovskite exhibits uniform elemental distribution, a key attribute of the high-entropy design. Crucially, the entropic stabilization in the CaNdY effect suppresses Sr diffusion, leading to improved chemical stability against both the YSZ electrolyte and Cr-containing interconnects compared to the benchmark oxygen electrode material (La0.6Sr0.4)(Co0.2Fe0.8)O3–δ (LSCF). While CaNdY exhibits lower electronic conductivity (∼80 S/cm) at 800 °C than the LSCF (∼261 S/cm), it maintains sufficient conductivity for charge transport and compatible thermal expansion coefficients. In SOECs, the CaNdY oxygen electrode delivers higher current densities than the state-of-the-art LSCF at &gt;700 °C, and it demonstrates less degradation for a 500-h stability test. Taken together, this work establishes that the high-entropy design can maintain electrochemical activity while reducing degradation, offering a promising pathway towards highly durable and efficient SOECs.</jats:p>
title: Enhancing Durability and Performance in SOECs with a High-Entropy Perovskite Oxide Air Electrode

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We present a high-repetition-rate experimental platform for proton stopping-power measurements in warm dense matter (WDM) in a regime where the projectile velocity approaches the electron thermal velocity and theoretical predictions remain highly uncertain. The platform combines laser-driven proton generation via target normal sheath acceleration with a compact magnetic energy selector to produce quasi-monoenergetic proton beams in the 0.3–0.6 MeV range with energy bandwidths of tens of keV and sub-nanosecond duration. WDM is generated by femtosecond laser heating of thin carbon foils and characterized using streaked optical pyrometry and x-ray pinhole grating spectroscopy, supported by radiation-hydrodynamic simulations. We investigate the present limitations of the approach, including uncertainties in sample conditions, finite proton bunch duration, and proton scattering, and discuss pathways toward improved measurements. The results demonstrate a versatile and scalable approach for systematic, high-statistics studies of ion stopping power in WDM relevant to inertial confinement fusion and charged-particle transport in high-energy-density plasmas.</jats:p>
title: Platform for high repetition rate proton stopping power measurements in warm dense matter

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Anion-derived inorganic-rich cathode-electrolyte interphases (CEIs) offer a promising solution for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries. However, conventional electrolytes struggle to suppress parasitic side reactions at the high-voltage cathode interface. Herein, a principle for ion pair acceptor electrolyte (IPAE) is proposed utilizing phosphazene-based molecules. Leveraging both anion-π and ion-dipole interactions, tailored (trifluoroethoxy)pentafluorocyclotriphosphazene (TFPN) interacts moderately with Li+ and anions. These coordinations promote the formation of compact Li⁺-TFPN-anion nano-clusters in the electrolyte and facilitate a uniform, thin CEI during initial charging. The resulting interphase alleviates oxygen evolution and inhibits surface structural degradation, enabling the lithium-rich battery with 80% capacity retention over 1000 cycles. Furthermore, the IPAE enables a high energy density of 514 Wh kg−1 in a Li||LLO pouch cell with stable cycling. This work establishes a general design principle for high-performance electrolytes and an effective interphase engineering strategy for high-energy-density batteries with extended cycle life.</jats:p>
title: Ion pair acceptor electrolyte for high-energy Li-rich batteries

items.abstract: <jats:p>The evolving nature of terrorism in West Africa has underscored the importance of intelligence-led counterterrorism strategies capable of addressing increasingly sophisticated and transnational threats. Violent extremist organisations, such as Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), Boko Haram, and other affiliated armed groups, continue to exploit porous borders, weak institutional coordination, limited intelligence interoperability, and governance deficits to expand their operational reach across the region. Although West African states have established various national and regional mechanisms to facilitate intelligence collection, analysis, and dissemination, persistent challenges associated with institutional fragmentation, political mistrust, legal constraints, technological disparities, and resource limitations continue to undermine effective intelligence sharing. This paper examines the strategic role of national and regional fusion centres in enhancing counterterrorism intelligence cooperation across West Africa. Drawing on secondary data, the paper evaluates existing intelligence-sharing frameworks, identifies operational challenges, and proposes practical strategies for strengthening intelligence fusion mechanisms. The study argues that effective intelligence fusion centres can enhance situational awareness, improve coordination, strengthen early-warning systems, and facilitate collective responses, thereby increasing regional resilience against terrorism and promoting lasting peace and security in West Africa.</jats:p>
title: Enhancing counterterrorism intelligence and information sharing: Strengthening regional and national fusion Centers in West Africa

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The sluggish desolvation of Zn
                    <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                    within carbon nanopores and the limited thickness of electrical double layer (EDL) severely restrict the space charge density and energy storage capability of zinc‐ion hybrid capacitors (ZIHCs). To address this, we propose a pretreatment strategy based on recycled H
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    PO
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    leaching to fabricate porous carbon materials that enable gradient charge storage. This method harnesses the dehydrating effect of H
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    PO
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    to hydrolyze biomass into small organic molecules, which subsequently undergo polymerization and activation, yielding carbon materials. Notably, the resulting carbon features hierarchically confined micropores (0.86–2 nm) that impose a spatial confinement effect on [Zn(H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O)
                    <jats:sub>6</jats:sub>
                    ]
                    <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                    , while P/O functional groups serve as catalytic desolvation sites. These sites synergistically enhance Zn
                    <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                    adsorption and hierarchically lower the desolvation energy barrier, thereby inducing the formation of a compact EDL and substantially boosting the space charge density. Consequently, BC‐2 delivers outstanding ZIHC performance, including a high specific capacity of 294.8 mAh g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , a battery‐level energy density of 235.83 Wh kg
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , and exceptional long‐term cycling stability (50 000 cycles, 103.58% retention). Theoretical calculations and kinetic analyses further elucidate the synergistic mechanism by which hierarchically confined micropores and P/O functional groups facilitate gradient charge storage and interfacial desolvation. This approach offers a green route toward ZIHCs.
                  </jats:p>

                    <sup>2+</sup>
                    Desolvation in Hierarchically Confined Carbon Enabled by Recycled H
                    <sub>3</sub>
                    PO
                    <sub>4</sub>

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Efficient volatile iodine uptake and release is crucial for nuclear waste remediation and aerospace propulsion. However, current sorbents often face a trade-off between high capacity and facile regeneration, as strong host–guest interactions can hinder low-energy iodine release. Here, we report a reticular chemistry strategy combining geometry-driven confinement and structural retrofitting to address this challenge. In MOF-521, favorable geometric matching between one-dimensional rhombic channels and I2 molecules promotes dense iodine confinement, achieving an intrapore packing density of 3.18 g·cm−3 and utilizing approximately 65% of the available pore space. Comprehensive investigations integrating single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), Raman and XPS spectroscopy, electrical conductivity measurements, and theoretical calculations reveal a dual-stage synergistic capture mechanism. Initial iodine incorporation involves speciation evolution and charge redistribution, followed by progressive geometry-confined physical filling and dense iodine organization. SCXRD further resolves ordered iodine assemblies with short I···I contact, highlighting the role of spatial confinement in promoting dense packing. However, such confined packing also contributes to framework deformation during desorption. Replacing monodentate formate with ditopic fumarate yields MOF-521-Fum with a distinct wwq topology. This structural retrofit maintains a high intrapore packing density of 2.79 g·cm−3, raises the decomposition temperature by 200 °C, enables complete iodine desorption, and achieves 96% capacity retention after four cycles. These findings highlight geometry-driven confinement and targeted structural regulation as complementary strategies for balancing dense iodine storage and reversible release.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Geometry-driven confinement and iodine evolution in robust metal–organic frameworks for adsorptive iodine storage

items.abstract: <jats:p>Energy storage reduces energy imbalances between supply and demand by capturing it at one time and storing it for later use. The term “battery” or “accumulator” refers to a device that stores electrical energy. Power grid stability, reliability, and acceptable operations are challenges associated with integrating renewable energy sources into the power grid. Energy storage systems (ESSs) can supplement power grids in handling unpredictable loads. The location, type of energy source, cost, and its environmental impact play a major role in the implementation of an ESS. There are different types of ESS currently in use, including some others that are under development, as presented in this paper. Due to the availability of a wide range of storage technologies, each offering a different scale of power, response time, energy density, discharge duration, and cost, it remains a challenge to select a storage system that is suitable for a particular application. A comparative analysis presented in this paper provides a clear picture of the suitability of different types of ESS for various applications, especially those related to distributed energy systems. Additionally, this will help the researchers in identifying the one for future research.</jats:p>
title: A critical review of the classification and application of energy storage systems in distributed energy systems incorporating renewable energy sources

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    A new gyrokinetic code,
                    <jats:monospace>TEK</jats:monospace>
                    , was benchmarked in simulating energetic particle (EP) driven toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes (TAEs) in the simple tokamak configuration chosen by the ITPA-EP group for code benchmarking purposes. Linear benchmark has been well established by other codes, whereas nonlinear benchmark for this case is lacking. This paper presents, besides the linear benchmark, nonlinear results for both single-
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>
                        
                      </jats:tex-math>
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mrow>
                          <mml:mi>n</mml:mi>
                        </mml:mrow>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    and multiple-
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>
                        
                      </jats:tex-math>
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mrow>
                          <mml:mi>n</mml:mi>
                        </mml:mrow>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    simulations (
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>
                        
                      </jats:tex-math>
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mrow>
                          <mml:mi>n</mml:mi>
                        </mml:mrow>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    is the toroidal mode number). The nonlinear results are in good agreement with an analytical theory on zonal field beat-driven by Alfvén eigenmodes, partially verifying the correctness of the nonlinear simulations. The saturation level and the resulting EP transport are examined. This provides data for future inter-code nonlinear benchmarking. In
                    <jats:monospace>TEK</jats:monospace>
                    , all species (electrons, thermal ions, EPs) are treated on the same footing using the gyrokinetic model (with electrons in the zero Larmor radius limit). The electromagnetic cancellation problem is mitigated by using the mixed-variable pullback method. Numerical details related to electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulation are discussed.
                  </jats:p>
title: Linear and nonlinear benchmark of gyrokinetic simulation of energetic particle driven toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes in ITPA TAE benchmark case

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates spatial segregation in "swarm" sounds, a class of auditory textures arising from multiples of rhythmic sound elements modeled on collective swarm dynamics in nature. Such sounds provide a controlled framework, inspired by naturally occurring textures, for exploring how rhythmic signals can be detected within dense auditory textures. Using ensembles of metronomes to approximate such swarms, we examined how density and spatial separation affect listeners' ability to detect and synchronize with an embedded target rhythm. Thirteen participants tapped along with a target metronome presented at varying azimuthal angles (0° to 65°) relative to a swarm masker directly ahead, with density varied across ten levels (200 to 920 sources). Detection probability increased with angular separation and decreased with swarm density, with a significant detection interaction suggesting that denser textures expand the spatial masking region. At low densities, reliable detection occurred at approximately 21°, while higher densities required separations of 29° or greater. Synchronization accuracy, measured via normalized inter-tap intervals, was reduced near the detection threshold, and reaction times increased under challenging spatial conditions. In general, the findings indicate that spatial position and source density jointly shape the extent to which rhythmic targets can be detected by sensorimotor synchronization.</jats:p>
title: Detecting Rhythmic Signals in "Swarm" Auditory Textures: Effects of Source Position, Density, and Synchronization Ability

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) are ideal candidates for all-solid-state supercapacitors (SSCs) due to their effective mitigation of leakage and volatilization associated with liquid electrolytes. However, conventional GPEs still suffer from flammability, low ionic conductivity, and insufficient mechanical strength. To address these challenges, this work develops a sodium alginate/polyacrylamide interpenetrating network (SA/PAM-IPN) incorporating Ca2+-induced “egg-box” ionic crosslinking and hydroxyl-rich coal fly ash (AWCFA) reinforcement, forming a multilevel synergistic network of covalent crosslinking, ionic coordination, and inorganic enhancement. Systematic KCl concentration studies identify 2.0 M as optimal, achieving ionic conductivity of 135.993 mS cm−1, areal capacitance of 779.625 mF cm−2, and nearly 100% capacitance retention after 30,000 cycles. Flame retardancy tests show significantly reduced peak heat release rate (HRR = 70.2 kW m−2), total heat release (THR = 4.4 MJ m−2), and total smoke production (TSP = 0.2 m2 kg−1). Density functional theory calculations reveal that enhanced surface negative potential and reduced HOMO–LUMO gap underpin efficient K+ transport, consistent with experimental observations. This study provides a multilevel synergistic strategy for designing high-safety, high-conductivity flexible GPEs and demonstrates resource utilization of industrial coal fly ash, offering guidance for the development of flexible energy storage devices.</jats:p>
title: Coal Fly Ash-Reinforced Flame-Retardant Interpenetrating Network Gel Electrolyte with High Ionic Conductivity for Flexible All-Solid-State Supercapacitors

items.abstract: <jats:p>Environment-perception modules underpin autonomous driving system operation for complex road scene comprehension. Three-dimensional (3D) object detection completes localization and classification work for road traffic participants including vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists. Camera sensors deliver rich texture and semantic data with performance degradation under low-light, fog and heavy-rain conditions. Millimeter-wave radar supports all-weather range and radial-velocity measurement with sparse point-cloud output and limited semantic discrimination capacity. Multi-modal fusion technology leverages complementary sensor characteristics for perception robustness improvement. This paper conducts millimeter-wave radar analysis covering historical evolution, working principle and core sensor characteristics. It compares sensor complementary attributes and three mainstream fusion paradigms, namely data-level, decision-level and feature-level fusion, to build the analysis basis for representative bird's-eye view (BEV) based Transformer cross-attention fusion networks. Technical bottlenecks covering space-time misalignment, modality imbalance and computing overhead are sorted out for subsequent discussion of practical engineering constraints and promising research directions in this field. Engineering-oriented suggestions are finally provided covering online calibration, model compression, physical-prior embedding and adverse-weather data augmentation.</jats:p>
title: Millimeter‑Wave Radar and Camera Multi‑modal Fusion for 3D Object Detection in Autonomous Driving

items.abstract: <jats:p>Positive Energy Districts (PEDs) have emerged as a transformative paradigm for urban decarbonization, yet their implementation requires integration across energy systems, buildings, mobility, and information and communication technologies, for which no coherent international standardization framework currently exists. This conceptual analysis examines the PED standardization landscape using a three-layer interoperability model encompassing technical, governance, and social dimensions. The initial standard inventory was primarily sourced from the IEC Technology Report Positive Energy Districts, supplemented by documents from SET Plan IWG 3.2, JPI Urban Europe, and IEA framework definitions. PED-relevant standards were defined as documents addressing energy, the built environment, mobility, digital infrastructure, or urban governance within district-scale decarbonisation. The analysis drew on the inventory documented in the IEC Technology Report, supplemented by the framework documents noted above. Standards were coded against the three-layer interoperability framework using the definitions and decision rules described in the Methods. Because the analysis is based on a documented inventory rather than an independent systematic search, statements about coverage and absence refer to that inventory. The findings reveal a pronounced asymmetry: technical interoperability is extensively but fragmentedly covered, governance interoperability is selectively addressed at a high level, and social interoperability is almost entirely absent. This imbalance reflects institutional path dependencies, including the historical division of standardization work, the technical composition of SDO epistemic communities, and an epistemology privileging codifiable, measurable aspects of systems. Technical interoperability is thus necessary but insufficient for PED success, which also requires governance and social interoperability that current standards do not provide. To address these gaps, the paper proposes orchestrative standardization, characterized by cross-domain mapping, process orientation, multi-level integration, and stakeholder-oriented design, and identifies the recently established ISO/IEC JTC 4 as a critical institutional opportunity. Theoretical contributions include a three-layer interoperability model extending beyond the technical focus of most interoperability research, orchestrative standardization as a framework for supporting sociotechnical system transitions, and institutional theory’s value for understanding standards landscapes. The paper concludes with implications for standards policy and practice, emphasizing the need for a formal PEDs standards roadmap translating identified gaps into priority work items with assigned responsibilities and timelines.</jats:p>
title: Standardization landscape for positive energy districts: mapping SDOs, gaps, and recommendations for interoperability

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Tailoring the Li+ solvation shell is a central design principle for many emerging Li metal battery electrolytes but remains largely qualitative. Here, we introduce a mean-field Ising model that predicts the Li+ solvation shell from the donor number (DN), acceptor number, molar ratio, and molecular size. The model is end-to-end differentiable, enabling direct parameterization from molecular dynamics (MD) solvation structures. For localized high-concentration electrolytes, it reproduces MD shell compositions with 10.7% RMSE at much reduced cost and captures solvation trends in other electrolyte classes without re-fitting. Model interaction terms show that DN dominates Li+ solvation energetics, explaining the empirical DN-based design rules. For LiTFSI in tetraglyme absent from training, the model identifies fluorobenzene as a diluent and a concentration window with anion-rich solvation shells and low free solvent. The predicted solvation structure is confirmed by MD, and published experiments on related electrolytes support the design principles.</jats:p>
title: Differentiable Solvation Shell Model for Rational Electrolyte Design

                  <jats:p>
                    Based on the energy confinement time scaling law of stellarator in the low-confinement mode, combined with energy balance equation and the plasma propagation and power deposition equations of the electron cyclotron wave in the three-dimensional magnetic field, a stellarator plasma start-up model including electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) and impurity radiation power loss is established. Validation against W7–X experimental data demonstrates good agreement in the temporal evolution of electron temperature and radiation losses, which verified that the model can correctly give the plasma start-up results of the stellarator under ECRH. This model is applied to predict the results of plasma start-up under 28 GHz ECRH for China Helical Device 1 (CN-H1) stellarator. The effects of the initial electron-to-ion temperature ratio (

                    on start-up are systematically studied and analyzed. The results show that the initial

                  <jats:p>
                    A new gyrokinetic code,
                    <jats:monospace>TEK</jats:monospace>
                    , was benchmarked in simulating energetic particle (EP) driven toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes (TAEs) in the simple tokamak configuration chosen by the ITPA-EP group for code benchmarking purposes. Linear benchmark has been well established by other codes, whereas nonlinear benchmark for this case is lacking. This paper presents, besides the linear benchmark, nonlinear results for both single-

                    simulations (

                    is the toroidal mode number). The nonlinear results are in good agreement with an analytical theory on zonal field beat-driven by Alfvén eigenmodes, partially verifying the correctness of the nonlinear simulations. The saturation level and the resulting EP transport are examined. This provides data for future inter-code nonlinear benchmarking. In
                    <jats:monospace>TEK</jats:monospace>
                    , all species (electrons, thermal ions, EPs) are treated on the same footing using the gyrokinetic model (with electrons in the zero Larmor radius limit). The electromagnetic cancellation problem is mitigated by using the mixed-variable pullback method. Numerical details related to electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulation are discussed.

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Markov state models (MSMs) are widely used to extract kinetic information from atomistic simulations, yet they remain largely opaque, requiring complex post hoc analysis to relate macroscopic states to underlying physical interactions. This disconnect severely limits the interpretability of the automated kinetic state decomposition. Here we introduce the Kinetic Interaction Tree (KinTree), an interpretable, interaction-centric machine learning framework for kinetic modeling. KinTree represents conformational dynamics in a feature space defined by noncovalent interactions and employs a decision-tree architecture optimized by a unified kinetic-structural objective function. This design enables the direct identification of kinetically relevant interactions while producing Markovian state decompositions from raw trajectory data. KinTree is validated across diverse molecular systems, demonstrating kinetic consistency through the Chapman–Kolmogorov tests and its ability to resolve mechanistic pathways. KinTree captures complex, concurrent inter- and intrachain interactions and sensitively identifies mutation-induced rewiring of interaction networks. By integrating kinetic modeling with physically interpretable features, KinTree provides a more highly interpretable and versatile approach for molecular interactions than existing kinetic models.</jats:p>
title:
Rule-Based Machine
Learning for Interpretable Kinetic
Modeling

items.abstract: <jats:p>Dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasmas have attracted considerable interest in a wide range of applications. However, different applications often require specific electrode geometries, and conventional electrode patterning methods can be costly and time-consuming. Here, we demonstrate a simple, low-cost method for fabricating DBD-plasma devices using 3D-printed contact masks. A poly(lactic acid) (PLA) mask produced by fused deposition modeling (FDM) was placed on a dielectric barrier, and conductive paint was sprayed through the mask openings to form the high-voltage electrode. The process requires no vacuum equipment, cleanroom facilities, wet chemical etching, sintering, or laser processing, enabling rapid modification and fabrication of electrode designs. Using a single mask, we fabricated comb-shaped DBD devices on glass, polyimide (PI) film, and 3D-printed PLA dielectric barriers. The design flexibility of 3D printing also enabled the fabrication of a kirigami-inspired DBD device that could be folded through 180° while maintaining plasma operation. These results demonstrate the potential of 3D-printed contact masks for the rapid, low-cost fabrication of application-specific DBD-plasma devices. The main limitations of the method are a coarser edge definition than screen or inkjet printing and the limited heat and erosion resistance of polymer barriers, which restrict the devices to burst-mode, short-duration operation.</jats:p>
title: Facile Fabrication of Dielectric Barrier Discharge Plasma Device by 3D-Printed Contact Mask

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Global (zero-dimensional or spatially averaged) models are widely employed to study complex chemistries in low-temperature plasmas (LTPs). By adopting a spatially average description of the plasma, they substantially reduce the computational cost while still providing reliable and detailed insight into the key processes taking place in the plasma. In their most general formulation, global models (GM) involve the coupled solution of a Boltzmann solver (to describe the electron kinetics) and a Chemistry solver (to describe the heavy-species kinetics). This paper presents a tutorial on the LisbOn KInetics Global Model (LoKI-GM) framework, developed in MATLAB and available as open-source code. The framework couples the Boltzmann solver LoKI-B, which solves the space-independent form of the two-term electron Boltzmann equation for non-magnetized non-equilibrium LTPs, excited by DC/HF electric fields or time-dependent (non-oscillatory) electric fields, and the Chemistry solver LoKI-C, which solves the system of zero-dimensional rate balance equations for the main charged and neutral species in the plasma and at the surface, receiving as input the kinetic schemes for the gas/plasma/surface system under study. Distinctive features of LoKI-GM include the closure of the model through charge neutrality, which yields the self-consistent maintenance field of DC and HF discharges, and the availability of several transport models for charged and neutral species. LoKI-GM can also couple a microkinetic mesoscopic surface model and a gas thermal model to the volume kinetics. We briefly present the formulation of LoKI-GM, including its numerical solution strategy, input/output parameters, and calculation workflow for both active discharges and afterglow plasmas. The main differences with respect to existing GM are highlighted, and the flexibility of the code for plasma chemistry studies is demonstrated through representative simulation results obtained across a range of gas discharge configurations and operating conditions.</jats:p>
title: LoKI-GM: a global model framework for plasma chemistry studies

items.abstract: <jats:p>Simulation-based medical education (SBME) curricula are used throughout the continuum of medical education. Graduate medical education (GME) now focuses heavily on achievement of milestones within a competency-based paradigm. SBME curricula should, therefore, demonstrate Kirkpatrick’s level 2 or higher improvement in competencies relevant to GME learners. This review characterizes the current state of SBME curricula for GME learners related to 6 core competencies described by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education. Most curricula address specialty-specific patient care and medical knowledge using task trainers. Much less commonly reported are curricula for nontechnical skills within professionalism, systems-based practice, problem-based learning and improvement, and interpersonal and communication skills. This review also revealed specialties that create SBME curricula and leverage simulation and the paucity of curricula across multiple programs or an institution. Creation of such curricula would fill a curricular void that currently exists and provide value for programs, trainees, and program leadership alike.</jats:p>
title: Scoping Review of Simulation-based Curricula in Graduate Medical Education

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study investigated the removal of sulfamethoxazole (SMX) from water using polyethylene terephthalate‐based activated carbon (PET‐AC) obtained from domestic waste PET bottles in a fixed‐bed adsorption process. The effects of initial SMX concentration (5–15 mg L
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ), adsorbent amount (0.2–0.6 g), and flow rate (2.5–7.5 mL min
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ) on adsorption performance were investigated. In addition, Thomas, Adams–Bohart, and Yoon–Nelson kinetic models were implemented to describe the breakthrough behavior. As the initial SMX concentration increased, the adsorption capacity increased, but the breakthrough time decreased. In addition, increasing the PET‐AC amount increased both the total adsorption capacity (q
                    <jats:sub>total</jats:sub>
                    ) and the breakthrough time. However, increasing the flow rate negatively affected the adsorption process. Furthermore, PET‐AC exhibited a higher experimental adsorption capacity (83.72 mg g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ) than commercial activated carbon (CAC) (56.04 mg g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ) under selected conditions (0.4 g PET‐AC, 5 mL min
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    flow rate, and 10 mg L
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    initial SMX concentration). Batch regeneration experiments demonstrated partial reusability of PET‐AC, with ethanol regeneration for 6 h providing the highest capacity retention (54.70%) after four adsorption cycles. In summary, this study offers an alternative perspective on addressing increasing PET waste while providing a promising strategy for removing SMX, which is difficult to eliminate using traditional treatment methods.
                  </jats:p>
title: Dynamic Adsorption and Kinetic Behavior of Sulfamethoxazole on PET‐Based Activated Carbon

<jats:p>
                    Residual capacitive coupling across insulating VO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    bridges can limit impedance matching in reconfigurable terahertz metasurfaces. This work numerically investigates damped kinetic-inductance compensation using two-layer graphene strips connected in parallel across these bridges. The analysis combines full-wave simulations, local equivalent-circuit analysis, and comparisons with purely resistive shunts and no shunts at identical device geometry. Graphene shunts increase the fractional bandwidth of the overlap between insulating-state absorption and metallic-state polarization conversion from 51.0% to 65.9%, whereas purely resistive shunts of 50−10
                    <jats:sup>4</jats:sup>
                    Ω/sq reach at most 51.3%. Over 2.166–4.296 THz, the dual-polarization absorptance and the polarization conversion ratio are both at least 90% at normal incidence. The circuit analysis shows that a purely resistive shunt adds dissipation without cancelling the off-state susceptance, whereas the kinetic inductance of graphene partially cancels it while retaining finite loss. This suggests a design approach for metasurfaces with predominantly capacitive off-state switches.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Bifunctional terahertz metasurface with damped kinetic-inductance compensation of the off-state capacitance of VO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    bridges

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>BACKGROUND</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The increasing demand for plant‐based proteins has intensified the need for sustainable separation technologies to recover protein‐rich fractions from agricultural by‐products. This study investigated froth flotation, a chemical‐free separation technique, to recover protein from broken split chickpea flour and to produce functional, protein‐rich ingredients.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>RESULTS</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The effects of operating parameters on protein recovery were investigated, and the optimum conditions were identified as a feed mass of 100 g, pH 7, an airflow rate of 8 L min
                      <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                      , and a flotation time of 20 min. Kinetic analysis indicated that the second‐order Arbiter model provided the best fit to the experimental protein recovery data. Under the optimum conditions, the protein concentrate achieved an enrichment ratio of 2.77 and a protein recovery of approximately 42%. Scanning electron microscopy and Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy supported the separation of protein‐rich and starch‐rich fractions, while differential scanning calorimetry indicated that the thermal stability of the protein was retained following flotation. The concentrate exhibited a water‐holding capacity of 2.67 g g
                      <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                      , an oil‐holding capacity of 2.18 g g
                      <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                      , a foaming capacity of 3.23 mL, a bulk density of 0.422 g mL
                      <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                      , and a tapped density of 0.53 g mL
                      <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                      .
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>CONCLUSION</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Froth flotation demonstrated potential as a simple separation technique for recovering protein‐rich fractions from broken split chickpea flour. The combination of protein enrichment, moderate recovery, and retained thermal stability suggests that the process could support the valorization of chickpea processing by‐products into functional food ingredients. Further studies on process optimization, scalability, and resource consumption are required to establish its industrial feasibility. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Optimization and kinetic study of chemical‐free froth flotation for waste broken split chickpea protein recovery

items.abstract: <jats:p>In recent years, targeted alpha-particle therapy (TAT), with its high linear energy transfer (LET) and extremely short tissue range, has gradually become an important research direction in precision radiotherapy for cancer. These physical properties enable precise irradiation of tumors while minimizing damage to surrounding healthy tissues. Although TAT has broad prospects for clinical application, its underlying biological mechanisms remain poorly understood. This review systematically summarizes progress in research on the mechanisms of TAT, with a focus on multiple forms of cell death induced by α-particle irradiation, including apoptosis, necrosis, pyroptosis, and other forms of regulated cell death. Alpha-particle-induced bystander effects and their double-edged role during treatment are also discussed. Recent advances in combining TAT with therapies such as immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) are further reviewed. Available evidence indicates that deeper investigation of TAT mechanisms not only reveals its multiple roles in cell death and immune activation, but also provides an important theoretical basis for combination strategies and the development of next-generation radiopharmaceuticals.</jats:p>
title: Mechanistic Insights into Targeted Alpha-Particle Therapy: Recent Advances

<jats:p>Objetivo: Determinar la correlación entre el Índice Aterogénico del Plasma (IAP) y el Péptido Natriurético tipo B (BNP) en pacientes con Insuficiencia Cardíaca Crónica Agudizada.


Material y métodos: Estudio transversal, correlacional, analítico. A través de un muestreo no probabilístico, fueron evaluados pacientes con insuficiencia cardíaca crónica agudizada, con medición al ingreso de BNP, perfil de lípidos y a quienes fue realizado un ecocardiograma transtorácico durante su hospitalización.


Resultados: Fueron estudiados 30 pacientes con insuficiencia cardíaca agudizada. La mediana de los niveles de BNP al ingreso fue de 764.5 pg/mL, la mediana del IAP fue de 0.51. La media de la fracción de eyección del ventrículo izquierdo (FEVI) obtenida fue de 38%, todos los pacientes presentaron algún grado de disfunción diastólica: el 50% grado 1, el 33.3% grado 2 y sólo el 16.6% grado 3. El coeficiente de correlación de Spearman para el BNP e IAP fue de -0,02213, con un valor de p=0.5.


Conclusiones: El IAP juega un papel como un factor de riesgo cardiovascular, pero no como parte de la evaluación de los pacientes con Insuficiencia Cardíaca Crónica Agudizada. No existe correlación entre el IAP y BNP.</jats:p>
title: Correlación entre el índice aterogénico del plasma y el péptido natriurético tipo B en pacientes con insuficiencia cardíaca cronica agudizada

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    German modal particles such as
                    <jats:italic>schon</jats:italic>
                    pose persistent challenges in teaching German as a foreign language because their discourse‐pragmatic functions are highly context‐dependent and lack direct equivalents in many learners’ first languages. Although learners frequently encounter
                    <jats:italic>schon</jats:italic>
                    in authentic input, including subtitled audiovisual media, its interpersonal and illocutionary nuances are rarely addressed explicitly in instruction. To examine the pragmatic input available to learners, this study analyzes 10,000 German–Korean subtitle pairs from the OpenSubtitles corpus. Instances of
                    <jats:italic>schon</jats:italic>
                    were categorized by illocutionary type (assertive, directive, interrogative) and six translation strategies. The results show that 82.6% of cases were classified as Pragmatic Omission (Strategy F) under the applied coding criteria, indicating that the function of
                    <jats:italic>schon</jats:italic>
                    was not overtly represented in Korean subtitles. A significant association between illocutionary type and translation strategy further indicates systematic variation across contexts. The study interprets these patterns as evidence of pragmatic reduction in mediated input and proposes corpus‐informed pedagogical strategies to support the teaching of MP‐
                    <jats:italic>schon</jats:italic>
                    .
                  </jats:p>
title: Teaching the Untranslatable: What Korean Subtitles Reveal About the German Modal Particle Schon

items.abstract: <jats:p>Congenital heart disease (CHD) comprises a diverse spectrum of structural abnormalities of the heart and/or great vessels that are present at birth, incorporating a broad range of anatomical and morphological phenotypes. The structural defects are believed to result from complex interactions of genetic, epigenetic, metabolic, and environmental factors. Although genomic and conventional multi-omics studies have expanded our understanding of CHD-associated molecular alterations, bulk-tissue analyses often obscure cell-type-specific changes and provide limited insight into how molecular disturbances influence cardiac developmental trajectories. The emergence of single-cell and single-nucleus multi-omics offers an opportunity to define CHD across multiple biological scales and cellular contexts. This review examines current applications of single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics, epigenomics, and complementary multi-omics approaches in CHD research, alongside evidence concerning mitochondrial genomic variation, gene expression, and functional alterations. We distinguish measurements obtained within the same cell or nucleus from computational integration of independently generated datasets, highlighting the complementary nature and limitations of these approaches. We further discuss challenges associated with sample heterogeneity, developmental-stage representation, technical variability, and the interpretation of mitochondrial signals as indicators of function or causality. Finally, we outline future directions involving developmental-stage-resolved profiling, patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell models, organoids, CRISPR-based functional studies, spatial technologies, and computational integration. Combining cell-resolved molecular profiling with direct mitochondrial functional assessment and experimental validation may help establish mechanistic links between mitochondrial alterations, abnormal cardiogenesis, and CHD susceptibility, ultimately supporting improved disease classification, biomarker discovery, and the development of mechanism-informed therapeutic strategies.</jats:p>
title: Dissecting congenital heart diseases through single-cell multi-omics and mitochondrial biology: current evidence and future directions

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Severe aplastic anemia (SAA) is a life-threatening bone marrow failure syndrome driven by cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs). Dendritic cells (DCs) play a key role in triggering and maintaining this autoimmune attack, but the molecular factors behind their abnormal activation are not fully understood. Immunometabolic reprogramming, especially toward oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), is a feature of activated immune cells, but its regulation and function in DCs during SAA development are unclear.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted proteomic screening on myeloid DCs (mDCs) from healthy controls, SAA patients, and patients in remission (R-SAA). Functional validation was performed using in vitro mDC models (both primary and THP-1 derived) with gene knockdown or overexpression. The mechanisms were explored via co-immunoprecipitation, ubiquitination assays, mRNA sequencing, and metabolic analysis. The impact on CD8⁺ T cell priming was tested in co-culture systems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>OXPHOS pathways were enriched in SAA mDC proteomes, especially involving COX6A1 and UQCRC1/COR1. We focused on COR1, a core subunit of complex III. Knocking down COR1 reduced mDC phagocytosis, expression of co-stimulatory molecules (CD80/86), and the ability to inhibit CD8⁺ T cell proliferation and perforin/granzyme B production. Mechanistically, COR1 depletion suppressed OXPHOS and increased glycolysis in mDCs. RNA sequencing showed a significant decrease in Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling pathways after COR1 knockdown. Follow-up experiments revealed that COR1 is functionally associated with TLR8-dependent responses, as activating TLR8 rescued the functional and metabolic defects in COR1-deficient mDCs. Additionally, we identified the deubiquitinase USP13 as a direct interaction partner of COR1. USP13 stabilizes COR1 by preventing its degradation via deubiquitination. USP13 knockdown phenocopied COR1 deficiency, impairing OXPHOS and altering TLR8-dependent mDC activation, whereas these effects were reversed by COR1 overexpression.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We describe a USP13–COR1–TLR8 axis that links mitochondrial respiration to innate immune sensing in DCs, supporting CTL activation in SAA. Targeting USP13 or COR1-related OXPHOS, or modulating TLR8 signaling, could provide new strategies to restore immune balance in SAA.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: USP13-mediated stabilization of COR1 regulates oxidative phosphorylation and TLR8-dependent CD8⁺ T cell priming in myeloid dendritic cells

items.abstract: <jats:p>Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by progressive alveolar bone resorption, in which inflammatory signaling and aberrant osteoclast activation are major drivers of bone destruction. Emerging evidence indicates that osteoclast dysfunction is governed not only by canonical differentiation signals but also by coordinated regulation of mitochondrial quality control and cell fate. Disruption of mitochondrial quality control (MQC) under inflammatory and oxidative stress can lead to mitochondrial damage, reactive oxygen species accumulation, and metabolic dysregulation, thereby promoting multiple forms of regulated cell death (RCD), including necroptosis, apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, cuproptosis, and disulfidptosis. Conversely, oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and metabolic perturbations associated with RCD may further compromise mitochondrial function, suggesting bidirectional crosstalk between MQC and RCD. This review systematically examines the mechanisms through which the MQC–RCD axis regulates osteoclast function and contributes to inflammatory periodontal bone destruction, with particular emphasis on osteoclast fate and alveolar bone homeostasis. We further discuss therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial homeostasis, regulated cell death, and inflammatory signaling, together with emerging precision delivery approaches, and highlight current knowledge gaps and translational opportunities for preventing periodontitis-associated bone loss.</jats:p>
title: Interplay between mitochondrial quality control and regulated cell death in osteoclast function and periodontal bone loss

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Protein adsorption at mineral interfaces governs the environmental transport, persistence, and transformation of these biomolecules, yet the factors controlling these biotic–abiotic molecular interactions remain incompletely understood. Here, β-lactoglobulin (β-LG), a model globular protein, was used to investigate these interactions with several mineral surfaces, including hematite, goethite, rutile, and kaolinite, at an environmentally relevant pH of 6. By integrating vibrational spectroscopy and mass spectrometry, we have determined that there are both conformational changes of the protein and oxidation of protein residues. The extent of oxidation depends on specific mineral interactions, with adsorption of β-LG on hematite causing the greatest amount of protein oxidation. Additionally, Attenuated Total Reflectance Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy clearly shows spectral changes in the amide I and amide II bands for adsorbed β-LG. Analysis of the bands reveals that although mineral surfaces oxidized β-LG to varying degrees, all of the mineral surface interactions result in a decrease in β-sheets with a concomitant increase in α-helices relative to solution-phase β-LG. Interestingly, the total adsorption capacity of β-LG on the different mineral surfaces at pH 6 did not follow a simple relationship with charge but instead showed a more complex dependence, i.e., an interplay between charge, surface area, and protein oxidation through mineral-specific surface interactions. Overall, through the integration of these different methods of analysis, we have been able to provide additional insights into protein–mineral surface interactions and the impact of surface adsorption on protein conformation and oxidation.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Small-sample datasets with high dimension often contain many redundant, irrelevant, and noisy features, leading to exponentially large search spaces, unstable population initialization, and insufficient use of task-related prior knowledge during evolutionary search. To address these issues, we propose CA-SAE-BPSO, a class-aware sparse autoencoder-assisted binary particle swarm optimization method with dynamic feature-prior guidance. First, a class-aware sparse autoencoder is trained by jointly optimizing reconstruction loss, classification loss, and sparsity regularization to learn task-relevant feature representations and derive class-discriminative feature priors. These priors guide a hybrid initialization strategy designed to exploit task-related information while retaining randomly generated alternatives. During evolution, the learned priors are dynamically fused with population-level feature selection frequencies so that the search gradually shifts from externally learned knowledge to population-accumulated search experience. A composite fitness function jointly considering balanced accuracy, subset size, and inter-feature redundancy is further introduced, together with a budget-limited single-bit-flip local refinement strategy. When features were selected using the full dataset before classifier cross-validation, CA-SAE-BPSO achieved the highest mean balanced accuracy on four of eight datasets and the lowest mean rank (2.5000) among nine methods. In a separate five-fold outer-test evaluation, in which test folds were excluded from feature selection, it obtained the lowest mean rank (3.6875) and shared the highest mean balanced accuracy on two datasets. The Friedman test did not detect an overall difference in the outer-test evaluation.</jats:p>
title: Task-Aware Prior-Guided Binary Particle Swarm Optimization for High-Dimensional Feature Selection

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Gassing polymers are widely used in low-voltage switching devices because their arc-induced ablation products promote arc cooling and post-arc dielectric recovery. However, ablation may also generate carbonaceous precursors and residues that deteriorate insulation performance. To link short-timescale atomistic reactions with long-timescale product evolution, this work develops a mechanism-informed chemical-kinetic framework for arc-induced polymer ablation. For PA66, reaction pathways extracted from multi-configuration ReaxFF molecular dynamics are parameterized through database matching, rate-rule estimation, and quantum-chemical calculations, and then incorporated into reaction mechanism generator calculations. A skeletal mechanism with 81 species and 191 reactions is reduced from a detailed mechanism containing 148 species and 967 reactions, while preserving the key product evolution over 1000–5000 K and 1–10 atm. The kinetic analysis shows that H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    is favoured at intermediate temperatures, whereas C
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    and other unsaturated carbon precursors accumulate during deeper decomposition. A yield-sooting-index-weighted carbon-deposition propensity index,
                    <jats:italic>
                      S
                      <jats:sub>CSI</jats:sub>
                    </jats:italic>
                    , is further proposed and applied to PA6, PA66, PA46, and POM. Experiments under three arc currents and three arcing durations show that
                    <jats:italic>
                      S
                      <jats:sub>CSI</jats:sub>
                    </jats:italic>
                    correlates inversely with post-arc partial-discharge inception voltage (PDIV) under severe ablation, while the correlation weakens under mild conditions. Cleaning experiments further show that PDIV recovers markedly after removal of retained surface residues, indicating that carbonaceous contamination is a major contributor to severe post-arc dielectric degradation. The proposed framework provides a quantitative link between atomistic ablation chemistry, carbon-deposition propensity, and post-arc dielectric performance.
                  </jats:p>
title: Mechanism-informed kinetic modelling of arc-induced ablation and carbon-deposition propensity in gassing polymers

items.abstract: <jats:p>Corrosion of mild steel in acidic media remains a major challenge in industrial operations, necessitating the development of environmentally sustainable corrosion inhibitors. This study investigated the corrosion inhibition performance of Dioscorea bulbifera leaf extract on mild steel in hydrochloric acid using complementary phytochemical, gravimetric, electrochemical, kinetic, and thermodynamic analyses. Phytochemical screening confirmed the presence of bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, tannins, alkaloids, saponins, phenolics, and terpenoids, which are responsible for the adsorption and protective properties of the extract. Gravimetric measurements revealed a concentration-dependent reduction in weight loss and corrosion rate, while the inhibition efficiency increased from 19.17% at 0.5 g L⁻¹ to 83.48% at 2.5 g L⁻¹, accompanied by a maximum surface coverage (θ) of 0.8348. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) showed a significant increase in charge transfer resistance from 32.1 to 253.8 Ω cm⁻² and a decrease in double-layer capacitance from 103.5 to 8.5 μF cm⁻², confirming the formation of a protective adsorbed film. Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) measurements further demonstrated a reduction in corrosion current density from 847.5 to 69.7 μA cm⁻², achieving a maximum inhibition efficiency of 91.8%. Kinetic analysis revealed a progressive decrease in the corrosion rate constant from 0.01234 × 10⁻³ to 0.00285 × 10⁻³ h⁻¹ and an increase in half-life from 54.14 to 242.65 h, indicating enhanced corrosion resistance. Thermodynamic analysis yielded negative Gibbs free energy values (ΔG°ads = −12.3 to −19.9 kJ mol⁻¹), confirming spontaneous adsorption predominantly through physisorption. The combined gravimetric, electrochemical, kinetic, and thermodynamic findings demonstrate that Dioscorea bulbifera leaf extract is an effective, eco-friendly mixed-type corrosion inhibitor for mild steel in hydrochloric acid, with inhibition occurring through spontaneous adsorption and the formation of a stable protective surface film.</jats:p>
title: Integrated Gravimetric, Electrochemical, Kinetic, and Thermodynamic Evaluation of <i>Dioscorea bulbifera </i>(Bitter Yam) Leaf Extract as a Green Corrosion Inhibitor for Mild Steel in Hydrochloric Acid

items.abstract: <jats:p>Osimertinib achieves durable disease control in epidermal growth factor receptor-mutant non-small cell lung cancer, yet residual tumor cells can persist and subsequently enable relapse. Drug-tolerant persister cells comprise heterogeneous, frequently reversible states sustained by adaptive signaling, transcriptional plasticity, metabolic remodeling, and altered cell-death thresholds. Short-term depletion of a persister population does not establish prevention of stable resistance, and clinical activity of a combination regimen does not demonstrate persister-specific eradication. This review examines how receptor switching, RAS and AKT signaling, YAP/TEAD activation, developmental pathways, and inflammatory programs cooperate to establish and maintain persistence. It further integrates these networks with chromatin regulation, lineage identity, redox homeostasis, stemness, dormancy, and immune clearance. Therapeutic strategies are evaluated according to biological dependency, treatment timing, and durability after drug withdrawal, while longitudinal tissue and plasma analyses are considered essential for distinguishing reversible adaptation from genetic escape and histologic transformation. A biomarker-guided framework focused on residual disease may facilitate the development of mechanism-matched combinations that delay resistance without imposing unnecessary treatment burden.</jats:p>
title: Signaling reprogramming in drug-tolerant persister cells: therapeutic opportunities to delay osimertinib resistance in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer

items.abstract: <jats:p>A previsão de demanda pode apoiar decisões de compras e controle de estoque em operações de comércio eletrônico. Este estudo investiga a aplicação de modelos de aprendizado de máquina para prever vendas diárias de produtos comercializados no Mercado Livre e relacionar as estimativas a sugestões de reposição. Foram utilizados dados de um relatório de vendas exportado em outubro de 2026, com seleção de três códigos de produto (SKUs). Após a filtragem de registros com status “Entregue”, as séries diárias foram construídas para o período de 26 de setembro a 25 de outubro de 2026. Foram avaliados os modelos de Regressão Linear e Árvore de Decisão, comparados a uma referência sazonal baseada nas vendas de sete dias antes. A avaliação reservou cronologicamente os sete últimos dias disponíveis para teste e utilizou MAE, RMSE e R². Os resultados variaram conforme o produto: a Regressão Linear apresentou menor MAE em dois SKUs, enquanto a referência sazonal foi superior no terceiro. Os valores de R² negativos em dois dos três casos, além do curto histórico e do pequeno conjunto de teste, indicam que as previsões são preliminares e não devem ser aplicadas sem validação adicional. A sugestão de compra foi calculada com margem de segurança de 10%, considerando o estoque informado. O estudo demonstra uma aplicação inicial de previsão de demanda com dados reais de uma operação de comércio eletrônico.</jats:p>
title: PREVISÃO DE DEMANDA EM E-COMMERCE COM MACHINE LEARNING
E-COMMERCE DEMAND FORECASTING WITH MACHINE LEARNING

items.abstract: <jats:p>The rich sentiment in passenger reviews is often ignored in Airline recommendation system which yields low interpretability and weak predictive power. In the present study, it is suggested that AIRRecNet (Airline Recommendation Network) be used as a multimodal deep learning framework to be trained to use textual reviews, numeric service rates, and categorical metadata to facilitate contextual airline recommendation. Two variant forms (Full AIRRecNet and AIRRecNet w/o Cross-Attention) exist in which the cross-modal attention is applied to align the features to fit and AIRRecNet w/o Cross-Attention which merely concatenates the features. AIRRecNet will outperform the existing baselines of Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM, and MLP, and a textonly DistilBERT, model trained and tested on 8,100 reviewed airline reviews (2016-2024). The Full AIRRecNet is the better (0.9321, 0.9311) in terms of accuracy and F1-score and the ablation variant is the better (0.9862) in terms of the AUC-ROC and a much quicker improvement. The outcomes of the experiment imply that the multimodal fusion is a rational approach to incorporate the latent sentiment-service dynamics that will determine the passenger satisfaction and transform AIRRecNet into a reliable and interpretable airline recommendation analytics framework of tomorrow.</jats:p>
title: Airline Recommendation prediction Based on User Ratings using Optimized Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models

items.abstract: <jats:p>This discussion provides an introduction to and survey of machine learning methods in econometrics, covering both predictive and causal applications. We first consider supervised machine learning for predicting or forecasting an outcome of interest, such as wages, credit default, or product demand, including penalized regression, tree-based methods, support vector machines, and boosting, followed by neural network architectures. Next, we discuss unsupervised learning, which aims to detect patterns in data without a predefined outcome variable, covering clustering methods that group observations by similarity and dimensionality reduction techniques that extract compact representations of high-dimensional data. We then turn to causal machine learning for treatment evaluation, such as assessing the impact of job training programs on employment or of price changes on demand, covering average treatment effect estimation via data-adaptive control of confounders using double machine learning, treatment effect heterogeneity analysis based on causal forests, optimal policy learning to target subpopulations for whom treatment is most beneficial, and reinforcement learning for dynamic treatment allocation. We also discuss the implications of artificial intelligence-generated variables for causal analysis. Finally, we provide an introduction to causal discovery, which aims to learn causal structures among multiple variables from observational data in a data-driven manner.</jats:p>
title: Machine learning in econometrics
