items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Quantum error correction (QEC) can be enhanced by post-selecting out runs that are likely to produce a logical failure, but the most accurate measures for that require costly decoder-level information. We introduce a practical, decoder-agnostic post-selection method that learns directly from syndrome data. The method trains a supervised classifier to distinguish between syndromes from low- and high-noise regimes, and then uses the classifier’s output as an abort score for new runs, without requiring logical-error labels, correction operators, or code-specific likelihood calculations. We validate the approach in three complementary settings: circuit-level simulations of the Gross bivariate-bicycle code, code-capacity simulations of the surface code, and experimental logical magic-state distillation data from the QuEra neutral-atom processor (Sales Rodriguez
                    <jats:italic>et al</jats:italic>
                    2025
                    <jats:italic>Nature</jats:italic>
                    <jats:bold>645</jats:bold>
                    620). In the Gross and surface codes, learned syndrome post-selection reduces the conditional logical error rate at a fixed acceptance rate, with performance comparable to syndrome-weight (SW) filtering. For the surface code, the learned classifier reveals a post-selection transition distinct from the conventional decoding threshold. In the experimental data, the machine-learning score outperforms SW post-selection and, when combined with logical-gap (LG) filtering, improves the output fidelity beyond using the LG alone. These results show that syndrome-only learning provides a scalable and hardware-compatible route to improving the reliability of QEC.
                  </jats:p>
title: Machine-learned syndrome post-selection for reliable quantum error correction

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Markov state models (MSMs) are widely used to extract kinetic information from atomistic simulations, yet they remain largely opaque, requiring complex post hoc analysis to relate macroscopic states to underlying physical interactions. This disconnect severely limits the interpretability of the automated kinetic state decomposition. Here we introduce the Kinetic Interaction Tree (KinTree), an interpretable, interaction-centric machine learning framework for kinetic modeling. KinTree represents conformational dynamics in a feature space defined by noncovalent interactions and employs a decision-tree architecture optimized by a unified kinetic-structural objective function. This design enables the direct identification of kinetically relevant interactions while producing Markovian state decompositions from raw trajectory data. KinTree is validated across diverse molecular systems, demonstrating kinetic consistency through the Chapman–Kolmogorov tests and its ability to resolve mechanistic pathways. KinTree captures complex, concurrent inter- and intrachain interactions and sensitively identifies mutation-induced rewiring of interaction networks. By integrating kinetic modeling with physically interpretable features, KinTree provides a more highly interpretable and versatile approach for molecular interactions than existing kinetic models.</jats:p>
title:
Rule-Based Machine
Learning for Interpretable Kinetic
Modeling

items.abstract: <jats:p>Brain tumors represent a heterogeneous group of neoplasms whose diagnosis, characterization, treatment planning, and follow-up require accurate interpretation of medical imaging. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to noninvasive assessment because it provides strong soft-tissue contrast across complementary sequences. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have increasingly enabled automated tumor detection, localization, segmentation, classification, grading, molecular prediction, and prognosis. This chapter presents a structured overview of ML and DL methods for brain tumor analysis, beginning with radiomics and classical classifiers and progressing to convolutional neural networks (CNNs), U-Net-based encoder-decoder systems, attention mechanisms, three-dimensional models, transformer architectures, and self-supervised learning. It discusses MRI sequences, preprocessing, feature extraction, training strategies, loss functions, post-processing, evaluation metrics, and representative benchmark datasets such as BraTS. Particular attention is given to the trade-offs between accuracy, computational cost, interpretability, data requirements, and generalization. Recent literature indicates continued movement toward transformer-enhanced U-Net models, multimodal learning, foundation models, and clinically oriented AI systems. However, differences among scanners, institutions, protocols, and patient populations remain important barriers to reliable deployment. Explainability, uncertainty estimation, external validation, fairness, prospective evaluation, and regulatory translation are therefore essential components of future research.</jats:p>
title: Brain Tumor Detection and Analysis Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning

items.abstract: <jats:p>We predict GameFi returns using adaptive boosting (AdaBoost), random forest (RF), eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM). Selecting 10 GameFi according to market capitalization, we use both traditional and direct proxies for investor attention, in addition to including trading and technical indicators as inputs. We find that including attention proxies markedly enhances the predictive accuracy of machine learning models for GameFi returns. Further research using SHapley additive exPlanations (SHAP) identifies that attention proxies significantly improve GameFi returns prediction.</jats:p>
title: Predicting GameFi with machine learning: Identifying the importance of investor attention

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In today’s digital world, internet use has become an integral part of students’ daily lives. Although the internet offers numerous benefits, excessive use may develop into problematic or addictive patterns. This study employed machine-learning methods to predict internet addiction among students at the University of Tehran based on personality traits and self-compassion dimensions. A sample of 458 students completed the 10-item Big Five Inventory (BFI-10), Neff’s 26-item Self-Compassion Scale (SCS), and Young’s 20-item Internet Addiction Test (IAT). Seven regression algorithms (Linear Model, GLMNET, CART, Tree Bagging, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost) were first compared using repeated nested cross-validation (five folds, three repeats) and were then re-tuned on a 70% training partition and evaluated once on the remaining 30% hold-out partition. Supplementary SHAP and sensitivity analyses, based on a Random Forest model re-estimated in Python with the same eleven predictors, were used to examine the direction, shape, and stability of predictor contributions. Random Forest was retained as the final model for subsequent reporting and interpretation. On the hold-out partition, it yielded R² = 0.27, RMSE = 10.88, and MAE = 9.01. However, its substantially higher training performance (R² = 0.89), its cross-validated performance comparable to that of the linear and elastic-net models, and the variability of test R² across ten additional random splits (0.08 to 0.28) indicate modest and split-dependent predictive accuracy. These results should therefore not be read as evidence that Random Forest, or machine learning more generally, is superior to the alternative approaches. Conscientiousness, neuroticism, isolation, and over-identification were consistently among the most important predictors across the permutation-importance and sensitivity analyses. SHAP analysis indicated that higher conscientiousness was associated with lower predicted internet-addiction scores, whereas higher neuroticism and isolation were associated with higher predicted scores; the contribution of over-identification was non-monotonic. Support for self-kindness and common humanity was weaker and less consistent across analyses. These findings illustrate the potential value of combining machine-learning models with interpretability and sensitivity analyses while highlighting the modest generalizability of the current predictions. The identified personality and self-compassion dimensions may inform future research, but the results should not be interpreted as evidence of causal or therapeutic effects.</jats:p>
title: Personality, self-compassion, and internet addiction: a machine learning perspective

<jats:p>
                    During their academic journey, especially between ages 11 and 15, secondary school students often face heightened stress due to increased academic demands, responsibilities, and future concerns, posing a significant risk to students’ well-being and academic success. To support students’ healthy development, it is crucial to understand the primary predictors of physiological stress markers in secondary school students’ lives. Although previous research has identified several individual predictors, little is known about how a broad range of psychosocial, demographic, and behavioral characteristics jointly contribute to the prediction of physiological stress biomarkers in adolescents. To model how up to 59 variables describing adolescents’ (
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                     = 83; Mage = 13.72 years; 48% girls) social, psychological, and school-related factors predicted their physiological stress markers (cortisol, alpha-amylase, oxidative stress, telomere length) in a cross-sectional study, a machine learning approach was adopted. Random forests and Lasso models were fitted for each biomarker using cross-validation. Random Forest models predicting salivary alpha-amylase (
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     = 0.006) and Lasso models predicting telomere length (
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     = 0.005) achieved significantly lower prediction errors than the corresponding baseline models. Feature importance analyses indicated avoidance of academic failure as the most important predictor of alpha-amylase, followed by parental support, stress and burnout, inclusion in classroom and social media use. Telomere length was primarily predicted by school track, followed by social media use, gaming, sibling count, and burnout symptoms. The findings identify motivational, demographic, social, and technology-related characteristics as potentially informative predictors of physiological biomarkers. However, the observed relationships should be interpreted as exploratory and model-dependent rather than evidence that individual characteristics act as stressors or protective factors.
                  </jats:p>
title: Identifying predictors of stress biomarkers in secondary school students using machine learning

items.abstract: <jats:p>Predicting academic performance before final examinations can help educators direct support towards students who need it most. This paper presents a research framework for student performance prediction using machine learning, developed from a postgraduate research proposal. The framework combines academic indicators, including previous examination marks, internal assessments, attendance, assignments and study habits, to classify academic risk. It describes data preparation, a comparison of interpretable and ensemble classification methods, and an evaluation plan that emphasizes recall for at-risk students rather than accuracy alone. A teacher-facing reporting interface is proposed to convert predictions into actionable academic support. As model training and institutional validation have not yet been completed, this paper reports a proposed methodology and anticipated contributions, not measured performance.</jats:p>
title: Student Performance Prediction Using Machine Learning

items.abstract: <jats:p>Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) pipelines remain the backbone of enterprise analytics, yet the transformation stage, and in particular data cleaning and data integration, is still dominated by hand-written rules, brittle scripts and expensive manual review. Practitioners commonly report that preparing data consumes far more effort than analysing it, and that errors introduced at this stage propagate silently into dashboards, reports and machine learning models. This research presents AutoETL, a modular machine learning framework that automates error detection, value repair, schema matching and entity resolution inside a single orchestrated pipeline. The framework borrows the Quality-by-Design (QbD) mindset from pharmaceutical development by defining a Quality Target Product Profile (QTPP) and Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs) for the curated output, and by controlling the pipeline through a measurable design space and control plan. Error detection combines Isolation Forest anomaly scores with a gradient-boosted classifier trained by uncertainty-driven active learning under a budget of only 100 labelled tuples; repair relies on chained gradient-boosted imputers; schema matching blends embedding, lexical and type similarity through the Hungarian algorithm; and entity resolution couples locality-sensitive-hashing blocking with an XGBoost pair classifier. Experiments on three cleaning benchmarks (Hospital, Flights, Beers), three entity-resolution benchmarks (Abt-Buy, Amazon-Google, DBLP-ACM) and a synthetic enterprise workload of up to ten million records show a mean detection F1-score of 0.88, a normalised imputation error of 0.221, a mean match F1-score of 0.81 and near-linear scalability, while Population Stability Index monitoring keeps quality stable over time. Paired significance tests (p < 0.01) confirm that the improvements over rule-based, ensemble and neural baselines are statistically reliable.</jats:p>
title: Automating the ETL Pipeline: Machine Learning Approaches to Data Cleaning and Integration

items.abstract: <jats:p>High-dimensional logistic regression extends traditional logistic regression by incorporating regularization techniques to effectively analyze complex datasets, particularly when the number of variables exceeds the number of observations. These methods enhance predictive accuracy by selecting the most relevant features. This study suggests two new penalized logistic regression approaches, Adaptive Ridge LASSO (ARLASSO) and Adaptive Ridge Elasticnet (AREnet), which enhance feature selection by incorporating Ridge penalty coefficients as adaptive weights in Adaptive LASSO and Adaptive Enet. The proposed methods are compared with existing approaches, including LASSO, Ridge, Elastic Net, Group LASSO, Adaptive LASSO, and Adaptive Enet, through various evaluation metrics. The results reveal that ARLASSO and AREnet achieve superior outcomes compared to existing penalized methods. Furthermore, we applied machine learning approaches, specifically Random Forest and XGBoost, to the features selected by the penalized logistic regression methods. These analyses were conducted through the simulation study, and the findings were validated using the Colon data set. The findings confirm that features identified by our proposed methodologies when integrated with machine learning models, deliver enhanced performance over directly applying machine learning models to the entire data set.</jats:p>
title: Enhancing Machine Learning Performance Using Penalized Methods in High-Dimensional Logistic Regression

items.abstract: <jats:p>Machine learning now reaches every stage of transcription factor (TF) drug discovery, but its contribution falls sharply along the evidence hierarchy. This review works through five tiers of evidence, from sequence and transcriptome through protein structure, cellular phenotype and chemical matter to clinical validation, and examines recent progress and the strength of evidence at each. Unified models can now predict binding, accessibility and expression within a single framework, and the definition of a ligandable site has widened from a static cavity to a transient conformational state, so disordered regions are no longer excluded a priori. The downstream tiers are far thinner. Molecular generation keeps improving geometric plausibility, but a unified benchmark shows that such metrics do not track the ability to produce active molecules, and no clinical intervention to date can be traced to substantive machine learning input. Missing trivial baselines and information leakage also make retrospective evaluation systematically optimistic. What limits machine learning at each tier appears to be the supply of verifiable labels more than model capacity. TFs sit upstream of regulation, so a single successful intervention may correct an entire downstream expression programme, which keeps them attractive for diseases that still lack usable targets and demanding as a test of algorithmic prediction. On this reading, further gains for TFs and other undruggable targets depend more on what each tier can be made to measure than on new architectures.</jats:p>
title: Machine Learning for Transcription Factor Target Discovery and Drug Intervention: Progress, Challenges and Outlook

items.abstract: <jats:p>Porphyry deposits are the primary global sources of Cu and Mo and a major source of Au. Yet, the fundamental controls on the relative abundance of Cu, Mo, and Au in porphyry deposits remain poorly understood. Here, we leverage global geological databases and a machine learning (ML) algorithm to investigate first-order geological controls on Cu, Mo, and Au ratios in porphyry systems from a data-driven perspective. First, association rule data mining of mineral assemblages identifies subtype-specific mineralogical fingerprints across hundreds of porphyry deposits. Second, supervised ML models trained on zircon trace element data classify deposits based on Cu/Au, Cu/Mo, and Au/Mo ratio thresholds, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis, a technique used to explain ML predictions, defines the dominant predictors. The zircon models achieve high classification performance and consistently highlight Yb/Dy, U, Th, Hf, and redox proxies (metrics related to oxygen fugacity relative to the fayalite-magnetite-quartz buffer [ΔFMQ]) as key features, indicating that pre-mineralization magma evolution strongly influences the relative availability and partitioning behavior of Cu, Au, and Mo. We interpret these results as evidence that magmatic preconditioning provides a robust, globally detectable signal in porphyry deposit metal ratios, even though hydrothermal focusing and precipitation efficiency can further modulate final endowments. The combined mineralogical and zircon-based framework together offers a quantitative basis not only for refining porphyry subtype classification but also for improving Cu-Au-Mo exploration targeting.</jats:p>
title: Controls on Cu ± Au and Mo concentrations in porphyry systems revealed by machine learning

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Childhood obesity is a major global health challenge with consequences ranging from early metabolic dysregulation to an increased risk of chronic disease later in life. Among early life preventive strategies, breastfeeding has received considerable attention because human milk contains diverse bioactive components that may influence metabolic programming, appetite regulation, immune maturation, and gut microbiota development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to explore the potential relevance of breast milk bioactive components in childhood obesity prevention by integrating mechanistic biological evidence with a literature-informed interpretable machine learning (ML) framework. The analysis was designed as a hypothesis-generating computational synthesis rather than a prospective clinical validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic literature search was conducted to construct a structured biomarker level dataset based on evidence strength, frequency of obesity related association, and direction of effect. A random forest model, supported by shapley additive explanations (SHAP) based explainability, partial dependence analysis, clustering, and interaction mapping, was applied to identify priority metabolic drivers and characterize their relative contributions within the analytical framework.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Within this computational framework, adiponectin, ghrelin, insulin, and leptin emerged as the most influential bioactive components associated with obesity-related relevance. Predictive importance was shaped by a non-linear interaction between evidence support and literature recurrence rather than by either factor alone. Finally, the findings suggest that the protective role of breastfeeding is biologically multidimensional and may reflect interconnected hormonal, epigenetic, microbial, and metabolic mechanisms; however, these observations remain hypothesis-generating and require validation in prospective cohorts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study provides an integrated computational perspective linking mechanistic evidence with interpretable computational prioritization of human milk bioactives. The findings offer preliminary support for the biological plausibility of breastfeeding as an early-life strategy for childhood obesity prevention, while highlighting the need for longitudinal clinical validation to translate these computational insights into actionable public health recommendations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Breast milk bioactive components and childhood obesity prevention: mechanistic evidence and an interpretable machine learning approach

items.abstract: <jats:p>Monte Carlo simulation has been a standard tool in financial risk management for decades, yet it converges slowly and becomes expensive when models are high-dimensional, when risk must be measured in real time, or when extreme market states matter. Machine learning has entered this workflow in three main ways. Deep importance sampling trains a neural network to learn the measure change that makes rare tail events more likely under the sampler, so the variance of value-at-risk estimates drops sharply for a fixed number of paths. Generative models, Quant GANs among them, synthesize extreme yet plausible market states; because the synthetic paths reproduce heavy tails and volatility clustering, they ease the chronic shortage of tail data. A third line replaces expensive pricing or loss computations with a trained neural surrogate that answers within milliseconds, a good fit for tasks that need repeated valuation. This study reviews the methods behind these three lines and their applications, including value-at-risk and expected shortfall estimation, stress scenario generation, credit portfolio loss simulation, and deep hedging. It also weighs the open problems. Black-box models remain difficult to explain to regulators under FRTB, tail regions are data-poor, and no accepted validation standard has emerged. This study concludes by arguing for Bayesian uncertainty quantification inside the simulation loop, validation procedures that regulators can accept, and evaluation frameworks that price the new model risk.</jats:p>
title: A Review of Machine Learning-Enhanced Monte Carlo Methods for Financial Risk Management

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Low-temperature operation imposes severe limitations on lithium-ion transport in battery electrolytes, yet the coupled effects of solvent composition and fluorinated additives in the cold-temperature regime remain insufficiently resolved. Here, we combine classical molecular dynamics (MD) and machine learning (ML) to investigate 1 M LiPF6 electrolytes containing ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), and EC/EMC (3:7), with 0–10 mol % fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), from 298 to 233 K. The coldest states are treated as simulated liquid-like trajectories rather than demonstrated stable liquids. MD simulations quantify Li+ self-diffusion, Nernst–Einstein (NE) and Green–Kubo (GK) conductivities and local coordination, while Gaussian-process surrogates model the NE and GK conductivities across composition and temperature. Cooling produces a pronounced transport penalty, particularly in EMC-containing electrolytes, whose GK conductivity decreases by more than 98% at 233 K, compared with 90–95% in EC-rich systems. Li+ self-diffusion activation energies are 0.49–0.54 eV for EMC-containing systems and 0.27–0.29 eV for EC-based systems. Within the EC family, 0–2 mol % FEC gives comparable cold-temperature transport, whereas 5–10 mol % FEC shows lower GK conductivity retention at the coldest simulated temperature (statistically resolved only at 10 mol %). The analyzed coordination channels remain solvent dominated, and FEC is depleted from the Li+ first solvation shell, acting indirectly on bulk transport. The Gaussian-process surrogates achieve composition-disjoint cross-validated RMSE values of 0.56 and 0.57 mS cm–1 for NE and GK conductivity. Within the simulated liquid-like trajectories, temperature and host-solvent composition dominate the bulk-transport response, with FEC acting as a secondary modifier.</jats:p>
title:
Low-Temperature
Transport in Li-Ion Battery EC/EMC/FEC
Electrolytes: Molecular Dynamics and Machine-Learning Modeling

items.abstract: <jats:p>Chikungunya remains a significant public health concern in India, a tropical and subtropical region that places the country among the top contributors to the global disease burden. This mosquito-borne disease shows a strong association with various climatic factors, i.e. temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind speed, including population density, area, and population size in shaping its transmission dynamics. This study aims to assess the nature and extent at which chikungunya is associated with these climatic and demographic variables across all the states of India using Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models. In this work, the chikungunya case data from 2018 to 2024 have been considered, and the models have been systematically tuned using nested grid search with cross-validation. The model performance has been analysed through five evaluation aspects: classification, outbreak sensitivity, spatial smoothness, error analysis, stability analysis, and bootstrap variance. This study demonstrates the comparative spatial forecasting of chikungunya case counts across India for 2035 using tuned RF and XGBoost frameworks. It further identifies the key environmental determinants shaping chikungunya transmission dynamics across India and also reveals the best-performing ML framework for a sparse-data scenario.</jats:p>
title: How Climatic and Demographic Factors Shape Chikungunya Risk across India: A Comparative Machine Learning Study

items.abstract: <jats:p>Introduction: Oral cancers are a significant group of diseases with high mortality rates due to relatively late diagnosis. Objectives: In this study, we aimed to develop hybrid deep learning-machine learning models that analyze clinical images for the detection of oral cancer and precancerous lesions, and to compare the multi-class classification performance of deep learning and hybrid deep learning-SVM approaches. Methods: A total of 243 intraoral images were analyzed, covering five tissue categories: oral squamous cell carcinoma, oral submucosal fibrosis, leukoplakia, smoker's tissue, and healthy tissue. Image preprocessing was applied, and models were evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. End-to-end classification was performed with three deep learning models (custom CNN, MobileNetV2, InceptionV3). Furthermore, hybrid models (CNN+SVM, MobileNetV2+SVM, and InceptionV3+SVM) were created by applying SVM to the deep features derived from these models. Model performance was evaluated using metrics such as precision, recall, F1 score, and balanced accuracy. Results: The custom CNN model has an accuracy of 98.35%. MobileNetV2 achieved an accuracy of 91.08%. InceptionV3 achieved an accuracy of 93.77%. The hybrid approaches yielded better results of 98.23% accuracy (0.999 AUC) with CNN+SVM, and 91.38% with MobileNetV2+SVM, and 94.04% accuracy with InceptionV3+SVM. All models showed AUCs greater than 0.98. Based on the research, by customizing CNN model gave the strongest performance with the lowest cross-validation variance (±0.33%). Conclusion: The custom CNN model and the CNN+SVM hybrid model have shown promising results in the classification of oral cancer and precancerous lesions with clinical images that have low data volume.</jats:p>
title: Hybrid Deep and Machine Learning Framework for High-Accuracy Multi-Class Oral Cancer Classification

items.abstract: <jats:p>Wearable computers and embedded interaction systems have changed contemporary jewelry into interactive systems that can sense users' actions and provide them with a feedback. In this research, a computational analysis system is designed by combining embedded interaction system for touch sensing, wireless sensor network for data collection, and machine learning to study interactive experiences in contemporary jewelry from wearable art point of view. An interactive brooch based on ESP32 microcontroller board with embedded touch sensing by MPR121, feedback provided by RGB LED, and wireless communication by Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) is proposed. In order to implement interactive actions in this prototype and collect behavior data related to task completion time, touch frequency, response latency, and error rate, a within-subject experiment with 48 participants is conducted to compare static brooch with interactive one in terms of usability, immersion, emotional expression, and wearing comfort. Random forest classification model with 300 decision trees is trained to classify high immersion and low immersion cases according to collected behavioral and experience features with five-fold cross validation. As a result of experiments, it was revealed that the proposed prototype increased the level of immersion from 3.29 to 4.10 and emotional expression from 3.21 to 4.25. The random forest model showed F1-score equal to 0.806 and area under ROC-curve equal to 0.872, while response latency was the most significant feature among predictors. Thus, the presented work shows how embedded interaction systems and machine learning can be utilized to conduct quantitative evaluation of wearable art experiences.</jats:p>
title: Embedded Sensing and Machine Learning-Based Interactive Experience Evaluation of Contemporary Jewelry from a Wearable Art Perspective

items.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Timely firefighting operations can be a key element in alleviating the consequences of a fire. The purpose of this study was to compare the effectiveness of machine learning algorithms in predicting the response time during firefighting operations.
Methods: In this applied research, the response time of 1,402 firefighting operations in Ilam, Iran, in 2022 was analyzed based on 29 parameters. To design and validate a predictive model for response time, several machines learning approaches were employed, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Generalized Linear Model (GLM), Deep Learning (DL), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), and Gradient Boosted Trees (GBT).
Results: Data analysis showed that the GBT model based on the RMSE, REL, and AE criteria with values of 1.38, 2.01, and 0.94 min, respectively, and the SVM model based on RE% criteria with a rate of 18.5% compared to other models has a better performance in predicting the response time during firefighting operations.
Conclusion: Since response time plays a crucial role in the outcomes of fire, it is recommended for the policymakers and managers of the firefighting and safety department to use machine learning models to predict the response time of firefighting operations and improve their preparedness and responsiveness during these operations.</jats:p>
title: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Response Time in Firefighting Operations

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Fused filament fabrication (FFF) has gained substantial attention in additive manufacturing for making lightweight functional structural components. However, the mechanical performance of FFF-fabricated parts is heavily impacted by several interdependent processing parameters, making accurate prediction challenging. This study aims to establish a precise machine learning-based framework to forecast the tensile characteristics of polyamide–carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites made using the FFF technique.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A thorough experimental data set was developed by systematically adjusting key FFF processing parameters, including nozzle temperature, layer height, infill density, printing speed and infill pattern. Machine learning models, particularly random forest, Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and Light gradient boosting machine (GBM), were created to predict tensile strength, Young’s modulus and elongation at break. Model performance was evaluated using the coefficient of determination (R2), and feature importance analysis was conducted to determine the most relevant process parameters.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among the examined models, XGBoost had the highest predictive accuracy, reaching R2 values of 0.998 for the training data set and 0.956 for the test data set. LightGBM displayed greater generalization ability for all three mechanical properties. The five-fold cross validation showed mean R2 values of 0.921 for ultimate tensile strength, 0.871 for Young’s modulus and 0.889 for elongation demonstrating the robustness of the models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis indicated layer height as the most important parameter, followed by nozzle temperature and infill density.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research includes various steps such as mechanical property prediction based on data, automatic hyperparameters optimization using Optuna, comparison of various machine learning models, multi-objective optimization by means of NSGA-III and explanation of the artificial intelligence model by SHAP. The suggested method markedly diminishes experimental workload and material wastage, offering a rapid and efficient instrument for optimizing processes and predicting mechanical properties in additive manufacturing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Machine learning based prediction of tensile strength properties of fused filament fabricated PA-CFRP composites

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Sn─Pb perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are highly promising for the next generation photovoltaics, yet optimizing their performance remains fundamentally challenging due to the complex interplay of multivariables. Because experimental optimization is prohibitively resource intensive, predictive computational guidance is urgently needed. Here, aiming for superior operational stability, we utilize all inorganic perovskites as a model system to develop a machine learning surrogate framework trained on a rigorously curated dataset of 9387 simulated devices. Benchmarking multiple algorithms revealed that the optimal XGBoost regressor achieved exceptional predictive fidelity with an
                    <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    of 0.9998. To transcend pure prediction and elucidate the underlying physics, we deployed interpretability analyses—including Pearson correlation, permutation importance and SHAP. Explicitly identified are bulk defect density, Sn─Pb ratio, and carrier mobility as the dominant efficiency bottlenecks. By visualizing the multidimensional design space via 3D scatter mapping, we constrained a global optimization algorithm to pinpoint an idealized theoretical maximum power conversion efficiency of 28.25%. Ultimately, this physics informed framework translates black box algorithms into an actionable, quantitative experimental roadmap, providing a highly efficient strategy to rationally optimize the Sn─Pb PSC performance.
                  </jats:p>
title: A Machine Learning Blueprint for High Efficiency All Inorganic Sn─Pb Perovskite Solar Cells

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Pervious concrete (PC) serves as a highly porous pavement material enabling water infiltration, stormwater runoff reduction, and groundwater recharge. PC properties are often governed by factors such as aggregate shape, size, and pore characteristics, cement content, water–cement ratio, and additives. Although machine learning (ML) has transformed the construction industry by predicting conventional concrete properties, studies on PC with additives remain limited. Thus, the major objective of this study was to assess the effectiveness of ML models and algorithms in predicting the target properties of PC mixtures, including compressive strength (CS), porosity, and permeability, based on random forest (RF), gradient boosting (GB), and artificial neural network (ANN) using a master database of 350 data points covering 78 mixtures. An independent 36-point external validation set was used to assess model generalizability. The input parameters used for developing the models included water-to-cement ratio, aggregate-to-cement (a/c) ratio, density, and additives such as silica fume and crumb rubber. Performance metrics indicated that RF and GB outperformed ANN during CS prediction, with test coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.79 and 0.80, and root mean square error of 2.04 and 1.97 MPa, respectively. Further, mixture-level out-of-fold R2 of 0.45 (RF) and 0.44 (GB) represented the unbiased estimates. All three models predicted porosity and permeability with good to excellent accuracy (R2 = 0.83–0.98). Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations-based feature importance analysis revealed that density dominated CS prediction, and the a/c ratio governed porosity and permeability, thereby corroborating the distinct physical mechanisms controlling the mechanical and hydraulic performance of PC. All three ML models predicted the target PC properties with very good to excellent accuracy; however, the RF model showed the narrowest expected difference range (d3s) for predicted PC properties. It is envisioned that the proposed algorithms in this study can be readily applied in practice by entering component quantities in the same format as the training dataset. Overall, this research study contributed to comprehending the PC properties better and will serve as the foundation for a computational and statistical framework in the future to facilitate a paradigm shift toward developing environmentally sustainable and resilient roadway infrastructure materials/systems.</jats:p>
title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Machine Learning Models in Predicting the Target Properties of Modified Pervious Concrete Mixtures

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study investigates the application of machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze and predict the influence of carbonization temperature on the erosive wear behaviour of biochar-reinforced polymer composites. Biochar was produced from waste orange peel particulates at different carbonization temperatures of 400
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$^\circ $$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    C, 600
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$^\circ $$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    C, and 800
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$^\circ $$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    C using the pyrolysis process. Composites were fabricated by incorporating biochar as filler material at varying weight percentages (10%, 15%, and 20%) into the polymer matrix. The erosive wear behaviour was evaluated using an air jet erosion test apparatus under different operating conditions, including impact angles (45
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$^\circ $$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , 60
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$^\circ $$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , and 90
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$^\circ $$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    ) and impact velocities (48, 70, and 82 m/s). An L27 orthogonal array based on Taguchi’s method was employed to design the experiments. To enhance prediction accuracy and validate the optimized responses, ML models such as support vector machine, random forest (RF), and decision tree were developed. Among the ML models, the RF model exhibited the highest predictive performance with an
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$R^2$$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    value of 0.835 compared to other models. The results indicate that the erosive wear loss decreases with increasing carbonization temperature, with maximum erosion resistance observed in composites reinforced with biochar produced at 800
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$^\circ $$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    C.
                  </jats:p>
title: Erosive wear behaviour of polymer matrix composites reinforced with temperature varied biochar using experimental and machine learning approaches

items.abstract: <jats:p>Convolutional neural networks support edge-vision applications with different network shapes and latency requirements. Network-specific streaming accelerators exploit layer overlap, while shared-engine accelerators offer flexible scheduling across layers. FlexStream-CNN combines a streaming convolution-pooling front end with a folded fully connected back end for low-latency inference within a fixed LeNet-style layer sequence. Independent per-layer parallelism controls the reuse of fully connected arithmetic lanes. Runtime registers control convolution windows, stride, channel masks, pooling operations, input dimensions, and fully connected output counts. Geometry-derived vector lengths connect Flatten to the fully connected layers within fixed storage capacities. A serial configuration interface updates these controls between inferences while intermediate tensors remain on chip. Quantization-aware training (QAT) supplies integer weights and activations for compact storage and arithmetic, with wider accumulators and signed classification logits. Together, these mechanisms separate per-bitstream parallelism selection from runtime operator configuration within a fixed layer sequence and storage capacity. On this architecture, an output-window cycle model explains the measured latency-resource trade-off: nine routed configurations span a 24.6-fold frame-latency reduction, from 243.8 to 9.91 μ s at 200 MHz, with the balanced reference point at 12.82 μ s and 34.57 effective GOPS.</jats:p>
title: FlexStream-CNN: a runtime-configurable streaming FPGA accelerator for CNN inference

items.abstract: <jats:p>The conditions that lead to casualties in residential building fires are a combination of several factors: vulnerability of the occupants, fire origin and spread, response to fire alarms, fire-service response and the effectiveness of protection systems. In this paper, explainable machine learning for casualty and loss prediction, interpretation of predictions, and active fire protection are discussed. The mixed variables and nonlinear relationships of the incident records can be addressed by tree models and ensembles. Training data distribution may change with resampling, which may help determine minority casualty classes. Neural networks are able to learn and model spatio-temporal patterns, but require larger datasets and more rigorous external validation. Nor do feature importance, nor SHAP, give causality. Another study has also been linked to a reduction in the risk of deaths when smoke alarms are present. Occupants with limited mobility may be protected through automatic suppression such as detector activated systems that do not need an occupant's response. However, research is hampered by class imbalance, regional variation, limited information on the status of the system and reliance on counterfactual estimates. Issues that need attention are consistent casualty categories, consistent evaluation metrics, validation across regions, use of model explanations in fire-safety decisions, and system reliability and the needs of different population groups.</jats:p>
title: Applications of Explainable Machine Learning to Casualty Risk Prediction in Residential Building Fires: Current Status, Roles of Fire Protection Systems, and Future Directions

items.abstract: <jats:p>Machine learning has become a central framework for analyzing high-dimensional biological data generated by genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, single-cell sequencing, and multi-omics technologies. However, predictive modeling is frequently limited by severe class imbalance, where biologically important populations including rare disease subtypes, uncommon molecular states, and low-frequency cell populations are underrepresented. Synthetic oversampling addresses this challenge by increasing minority-class representation, with the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) being the most widely used approach. However, conventional SMOTE assumes that geometric proximity reflects biological similarity, an assumption often violated in high-dimensional, nonlinear, and heterogeneous biological data. This review examines clustering-guided synthetic generation methods that integrate unsupervised learning before oversampling, which may help preserve local biological structure. We evaluate partition-based, density-aware, fuzzy, cluster-filtering, and representation-based approaches, emphasizing their mathematical foundations, computational assumptions, and applications in molecular classification, rare population analysis, single-cell modeling, and multi-omics integration. Key challenges including cluster instability, preservation of rare biological populations, synthetic data validation, and distinguishing of statistical rarity from biological significance are discussed. Finally, we outline emerging directions involving biological foundation models, graph-based learning, multi-omics representation spaces, and biologically constrained generative frameworks. These advances represent a shift from conventional data balancing toward structure-aware synthetic modeling that aims to preserve meaningful biological organization while improving predictive performance.</jats:p>
title: Structure-Aware Synthetic Data Generation for Imbalanced Biological Machine Learning: A Review of Clustering-Guided Approaches

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Sustainable urban mobility depends on accurate trip generation modeling for effective transportation planning. Conventional models often overlook complex nonlinear travel behavior relationships. This study systematically reviews machine learning applications for trip generation modeling. Saudi Arabia's transportation context receives particular attention throughout the review. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 were systematically reviewed using PRISMA guidelines. Literature searches included Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and IEEE Xplore databases. Study quality was evaluated using predefined inclusion, exclusion, and quality assessment criteria. Seventy-five eligible studies were synthesized through qualitative and comparative analyses. Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and deep neural networks generally achieved higher predictive accuracy. Performance varies across datasets, validation methods, and application contexts. Long Short-Term Memory networks, CatBoost, and Graph Neural Networks modeled complex travel patterns effectively. These models captured nonlinear spatial and temporal relationships better than many conventional approaches. Diverse datasets included household surveys, GPS trajectories, smart-card transactions, mobile phone records, and Internet of Things sensors. Multi-source data improved model robustness and prediction reliability across different transportation environments. Key challenges include data availability, privacy protection, model transferability, explainability, and computational complexity. A Saudi-specific framework integrates multi-source data fusion and explainable artificial intelligence. The framework also incorporates privacy-preserving analytics and Geographic Information System decision support. Future research should prioritize standardized mobility datasets, multi-city validation, and institutional collaboration. The proposed framework promotes sustainable urban mobility through efficient and evidence-based transportation planning. It also supports Saudi Vision 2030 by improving forecasting, infrastructure investment, and transportation policy development.</jats:p>
title: Machine learning-based trip generation modeling for sustainable urban mobility using a systematic literature review and a framework for Saudi Arabia

items.abstract: <jats:p>Thermal coupling among phase modules becomes a limiting factor as multiphase power converters move toward higher current and power density. This paper presents an electrothermal layout optimization framework for a four-phase Buck converter. First, an electrical loss model maps the converter operating point to phase-wise heat-source powers by accounting for RMS-current-dependent conduction loss, switching loss, gate-drive loss, and inductor loss. A thickness-averaged two-dimensional heat equation is then reduced to a thermal coupling matrix using a Green-function formulation and mirror heat sources for adiabatic lateral boundaries. The resulting matrix distinguishes self-heating from mutual thermal coupling and enables rapid temperature evaluation during layout optimization. An adaptive genetic algorithm minimizes normalized peak temperature and temperature dispersion, while enforcing geometric and non-overlap constraints. For a 48 V/12 V prototype operating at 30 A per phase, the optimized layout reduces the simulated peak temperature from 91.49 °C to 84.86 °C (a reduction of 6.63 °C) and the average temperature from 35.74 °C to 35.04 °C (a reduction of 0.70 °C). Infrared thermography gives a peak temperature of 86.8 °C at 25 °C ambient temperature, compared with approximately 91.5 °C before optimization. The reported optimized FEM peak is 84.86 °C. The proposed framework provides a physically interpretable and computationally efficient route for multi-hotspot thermal layout design in high-power-density converters.</jats:p>
title: Multi-Hotspot Thermal Layout Optimization for a Four-Phase High-Power Buck Converter Using an Adaptive Genetic Algorithm

items.abstract: <jats:p>This article introduces three proposed topologies, each an extension of the conventional DC-DC positive output super lift Luo converter (POSLLC). By incorporating a switched-inductor (SL) cell into the POSLLC, the three modified POSLLC topologies succeed to provide a high output voltage along with a significant voltage gain. A high-voltage gain DC-DC converter is a crucial element in renewable energy systems, particularly in photovoltaic (PV) applications. It boosts the voltage before the converter is connected to a DC load or an AC load through an inverter, since the output voltage from a PV module is relatively low. The proposed designs provide several favorable features, including the utilization of only one controlled switch, continuous input current, the availability of common ground between the input and output, and the generation of a positive output voltage polarity. The proposed three topologies can provide a voltage gain of 8, 14, and 15, in comparison with only 5 in the original POSLLC when the duty cycle is 75%. MATLAB/Simulink models were developed and simulated to evaluate the consistency of the theoretical results obtained.</jats:p>
title: Three Topologies of Transformer-less High-Gain Step-up Luo Converter for Renewable Energy Applications

<jats:p>
                    The central–eastern Kuqa Depression contains vertically superimposed Upper Triassic–Middle Jurassic coal‐measure and lacustrine source rocks, whose relative contributions to oils in different reservoir intervals remain insufficiently constrained. Clarifying these contributions is important for understanding spatial and stratigraphic variations in oil–source relationships within the region. An integrated geochemical approach combining total organic carbon measurements, Rock‐Eval pyrolysis, maceral analysis, kerogen carbon‐isotope analysis, GC–MS biomarker analysis, and compound‐specific carbon‐isotope analysis of n‐alkanes was used to characterize these source rocks and correlate them with oils from reservoirs of the Ahe (J
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    a), Yangxia (J
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    y), and Kezilenuer (J
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    kz) formations. The sampled source rocks vary in quality among lithologies, are dominated by Type III kerogen with subordinate Type II, and are mainly low‐mature to mature. Jurassic source rocks in the Tugerming area have
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>o</jats:sub>
                    values of 0.54%–0.89%. In central Kuqa, J
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    kz and J
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    y source rocks mainly record terrestrial higher plant input from swamp–coal‐bearing settings, whereas Upper Triassic and J
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    q source rocks show stronger aquatic‐organic‐matter signatures. In eastern Kuqa, J
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    kz–J
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    y coal‐measure rocks form the principal source‐rock assemblage. Oil–source correlations suggest that oils from the sampled J
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    kz and J
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    y reservoirs are mainly associated with Jurassic coal‐measure source rocks, whereas those from the sampled J
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    a reservoirs show a closer affinity to Upper Triassic lacustrine mudstones. Local mixed sourcing may also occur. These results suggest regional variations in the relative contributions of coal‐measure and lacustrine source rocks within the study area, with oil–source relationships potentially influenced by stratigraphic position and source‐rock type.
                  </jats:p>
title: Geochemical Characteristics of the Triassic–Jurassic Source Rocks and Oil–Source Correlation in the Central–Eastern Kuqa Depression, Tarim Basin, China

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Renewable power electric vehicle (EV) charging requires DC–DC converters with high voltage gain, low input current ripple and robust dynamic response to fluctuations in renewable generation. This paper systematically reviews interleaved DC–DC converter topologies and control techniques reported for renewable-fed EV charging applications from 2015–2025. A six-database search, supplemented by citation chasing, identified 209 studies included after deduplication, screening and quality appraisal, of which 73 were eligible for quantitative synthesis. Converter topologies are classified into seven families and control methods into fifteen strategies. Normalized performance indicators are used to facilitate comparison across studies with substantially different power ratings and operating conditions. The analysis yields three principal findings; First, ripple cancellation is bounded and depends on duty ratio and phase number rather than being an unconditional benefit of interleaving. A closed-form cancellation factor is derived and verified by simulation at thirty operating points, showing complete cancellation only when
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    =
                    <jats:italic>k</jats:italic>
                    /
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                    ; a four- phase design operating near
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    = 0.1 cuts ripple by only about one third relative to the single-phase case while requiring four switching phases. Second, reported efficiency improvements of resonant and soft- switching designs are strongly dependent on switching frequency, limiting the validity of comparisons that omit this parameter. Third, significant experimental reporting gaps remain: only one surveyed study evaluates conducted emission against a limit line, six report power density, and none report post phase failure performance. The review gives a topology selection guide with unified control comparison based on dynamic response, robustness, computational burden, implementation complexity, sensor requirements and hardware platform suitability. The analysis further relates the bandwidth limitations of PI control to the right-half-plane zero of the boost-derived plant. The review identifies wide-bandgap devices, learning based controllers with a stability certificate, fault tolerant operation and hardware-in-the-loop validation, with reported processor execution times as priorities for advancing interleaved converters toward practical renewable powered EV charging.
                  </jats:p>
title: Interleaved DC–DC converter topologies and control techniques for renewable energy powered EV chargers: a systematic review

items.abstract: <jats:p>The generalized Gamma–Lindley q-distribution is the Jackson q-analogue of the classical four-parameter generalized Gamma–Lindley family. We show that a single truncated moment of an order statistic characterizes it completely among all distributions carried by the geometric lattice on which it lives. The argument rests on a q-successor kernel, defined as the negative q-derivative of a power of the survival function. This kernel is nonnegative on the lattice, has total Jackson mass one, and gives the conditional distribution of the order statistic of a prescribed rank once the number of observations below a lattice point is fixed. Jackson integration by parts expresses the associated truncated moment through the survival function evaluated one lattice step to the left; the resulting first-order q-difference equation, iterated along the lattice, reconstructs the survival function without a normalizing constant. The characterization is necessary and sufficient, requires no nondegeneracy assumption on the density, reduces to the classical one as $q\to {1^{-}}$, and contains the Gamma, exponential, Lindley, Gamma–Lindley, and weighted Lindley q-distributions as particular cases.</jats:p>
title: Characterization of the generalized Gamma–Lindley q-distribution by truncated moments of order statistics

                    Working memory depends on gamma oscillations generated across sensory and prefrontal cortices. In primary visual cortex (V1), stimulus-locked gamma oscillations encode stimulus information, while in prefrontal cortex (PFC), persistent gamma oscillations maintain this information after the stimulus is removed. In schizophrenia (SZ), gamma power is reduced in both V1 and PFC, consistent with deficits in sensory encoding and working memory maintenance. Both oscillation regimes arise from a canonical microcircuit involving pyramidal neurons (PNs) and parvalbumin-expressing interneurons (PVIs). Yet, whether the two regimes are similarly or differentially vulnerable to synaptic alterations within this circuit in SZ remains unknown.                     </jats:inline-formula>
                    I strength. Each alteration produced larger gamma power deficits in the persistent regime than in the stimulus-locked regime. Applied together, these alterations interacted synergistically to reduce gamma power, with the persistent regime exhibiting a more pronounced deficit. Bifurcation analyses revealed that this differential vulnerability arises from a wider margin of oscillatory stability in the stimulus-locked regime, and that reduced I
                    <jats:inline-formula id="pcbi.1014374.e004">
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" id="pcbi.1014374.e004g" mimetype="image" position="anchor" xlink:href="info:doi/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014374.e004" xlink:type="simple"/>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" id="M4">
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mo>→</mml:mo>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    E strength additionally abolished the bistability required for the persistent regime. These findings predict that a larger magnitude of synaptic alteration is required to disrupt gamma oscillations in V1 than in PFC, consistent with postmortem reports of more severe alterations in V1 in SZ. Together, they establish a differential vulnerability model of cortical gamma oscillations in SZ, in which regional differences in oscillatory stability determine how much synaptic alteration is required to disrupt oscillations with distinct dynamics.
                  </jats:p>
title: Differential vulnerability of stimulus-locked and persistent gamma oscillations: Implications in schizophrenia

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Researchers rarely work alone: they work with colleagues within and between organizations on all organizational levels. They collaborate on a variety of research results beyond traditional publications. However, collaboration indicators in research assessment usually rely on a single source, focus on top-level institutions, and may focus on journal articles only. This limits what can be seen about collaborations within organizations, and for results such as data sets and software. This article introduces a multi-source, multi-level, graph-based approach to collaboration indicators using Ricgraph (Research in context graph). Publications, data sets, software, persons, and organizational information from multiple systems are integrated into a single graph. Collaborations are defined as shared research results connecting organizations via persons. They are quantified on top-level organization, as well as on faculty and departmental level, providing a concrete operationalization of multi-source, multi-level collaboration indicators for science-of-science research. Combining multiple sources substantially increases the observed coverage of collaborations, especially for data set and software collaborations (&gt;400% for sources in this article, compared to a single source). Multi-level collaborations overviews reveal patterns that are invisible at the top-level alone. These results illustrate how multi-source, multi-level, graph-based collaboration indicators can complement citation-based metrics in responsible research assessment and institutional evaluation.</jats:p>
title: Multi-source, multi-level, graph-based institutional collaboration indicators for research assessment with Ricgraph

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates spatial segregation in "swarm" sounds, a class of auditory textures arising from multiples of rhythmic sound elements modeled on collective swarm dynamics in nature. Such sounds provide a controlled framework, inspired by naturally occurring textures, for exploring how rhythmic signals can be detected within dense auditory textures. Using ensembles of metronomes to approximate such swarms, we examined how density and spatial separation affect listeners' ability to detect and synchronize with an embedded target rhythm. Thirteen participants tapped along with a target metronome presented at varying azimuthal angles (0° to 65°) relative to a swarm masker directly ahead, with density varied across ten levels (200 to 920 sources). Detection probability increased with angular separation and decreased with swarm density, with a significant detection interaction suggesting that denser textures expand the spatial masking region. At low densities, reliable detection occurred at approximately 21°, while higher densities required separations of 29° or greater. Synchronization accuracy, measured via normalized inter-tap intervals, was reduced near the detection threshold, and reaction times increased under challenging spatial conditions. In general, the findings indicate that spatial position and source density jointly shape the extent to which rhythmic targets can be detected by sensorimotor synchronization.</jats:p>
title: Detecting Rhythmic Signals in "Swarm" Auditory Textures: Effects of Source Position, Density, and Synchronization Ability

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The removal of cesium (Cs
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    ) from aqueous solutions in the presence of competing metal ions is an important challenge in water treatment. In this study, a montmorillonite‐containing polymeric composite was synthesized through gamma irradiation‐induced polymerization of sodium acrylate in the presence of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and N,N′‐methylene diacrylamide (MBA), followed by ultrasonic‐assisted incorporation of montmorillonite. The adsorption behavior of the prepared composite toward Cs
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    and Sr
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    was investigated using kinetic, equilibrium, and binary competitive adsorption experiments. The pseudo‐second‐order model provided the closest statistical fit to the kinetic data, while complementary kinetic models suggested the contribution of multiple mass‐transfer processes. Equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir model, which yielded theoretical maximum adsorption capacities of 102 and 50 mg g
                    <jats:sup>−</jats:sup>
                    <jats:sup>1</jats:sup>
                    for Cs
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    and Sr
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    , respectively. Binary competitive experiments demonstrated preferential Cs
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    adsorption, with the selectivity coefficient (α
                    <jats:sub>Cs/Sr</jats:sub>
                    ) increasing from 3.63 at pH 1 to 11.78 at pH 6. Regeneration experiments showed that, after five successive EDTA‐assisted adsorption–desorption cycles, the composite retained removal efficiencies of 93% for Cs
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    and 88% for Sr
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    . These findings demonstrate the potential of the synthesized montmorillonite–polymeric composite as a reusable adsorbent with preferential Cs
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    uptake in binary aqueous systems.
                  </jats:p>
title: Cesium Removal From Aqueous Solutions Using a Gamma‐Radiation‐Synthesized Montmorillonite–Polymeric Composite: Competitive Sorption With Strontium and Reusability

items.abstract: <jats:p>Outdoor gamma exposure rates were assessed at 15 designated locations within a construction-company site in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area, Rivers State, Nigeria. Exposure-rate measurements recorded with a radiation survey meter were used to estimate the absorbed dose rate in air, annual effective dose for an assumed outdoor occupancy pattern, a lifetime cancer-risk screening index, and coefficient-weighted organ-related indices. Recorded exposure rates were 0.012–0.015 mR h⁻¹ (mean 0.01393 mR h⁻¹), giving air absorbed dose rates of 104.40–130.50 nGy h⁻¹ (mean 121.22 nGy h⁻¹). Using an outdoor occupancy factor of 0.20 and a conversion coefficient of 0.70 Sv Gy⁻¹, annual effective dose estimates ranged from 0.128 to 0.160 mSv y⁻¹ (mean 0.149 mSv y⁻¹). For a modelled 55-year exposure duration and risk coefficient of 0.05 Sv⁻¹, the corresponding lifetime-risk index ranged from 0.352 × 10⁻³ to 0.440 × 10⁻³ (mean 0.409 × 10⁻³). Five sampling locations recorded 0.015 mR h⁻¹, seven recorded 0.014 mR h⁻¹ and three recorded 0.012 mR h⁻¹. The results provide a location-specific baseline for outdoor gamma exposure and a consistent basis for comparison with subsequent monitoring of construction-site environments.</jats:p>
title: Outdoor Gamma Exposure Rates and Derived Radiological Indices at a Construction Site in Obio/Akpor LGA, Rivers State, Nigeria

<jats:p>The objective of this study was to evaluate the potential of paw-paw seeds as a source of edible
vegetable oil. Sun-dried seeds (SDS) and oven-dried seeds (ODS) of paw-paw was subjected to
Soxhlet extraction using petroleum ether as the solvent. The physicochemical parameters of the
oil were investigated. Results revealed the parameters; Oil yield, Acid value, Saponification value,
Iodine value, Peroxide value, Melting point and Smoke point were 47.5%, 4.635 mg/g, 32.721
mg/g, 1.269 mg/g, 0.737 mg/g, 10.55 °C, 37.33 °C and 32.1%, 4.208 mg/g, 12.805 mg/g, 0.850
mg/g, 2.337 mg/g, 9.50 °C and 36.34 °C for ODS and SDS oils respectively. The oil from paw-paw
seed is a non-drying oil. It is edible and can be used as an edible source of vegetable oils. Its use
in soap making is also encouraged. As a waste-to-wealth project, processing paw-paw seeds into
oils could serve as a source of income to farmers.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:p>Diabetes mellitus is a long-term metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia,
which can lead to various health problem if left untreated. The quest for new, more effective, and
safer anti-diabetic therapies continues, with a growing interest in natural compounds derived from
medicinal plants. Among the promising natural sources, the avocado fruit has garnered attention
for its potential antidiabetic properties. Avocado peel was earlier reported to have higher alphaamylase inhibitory activities compared to other part of the fruit, thus suggested to possess
antidiabetic properties. Reported phytochemicals isolated from Avocado peel were subjected to
screening via molecular docking simulation using PyRx docking tool for visualization against
alpha-amylase and human glucosidase enzyme and ADMET profiling. The docking scores with
ADMET profiling reported three of the screened ligands: rutin (-9.4 kcal/mol), epigallocatechin
gallate (-9.3 kcal/mol), and delphinidin-3-O-glucoside (-9.0 kcal/mol) as very effective potential
drug candidates as compared to the conventional medications of diabetes, glipizide (-8.1 kcal/mol)
and biguanide (-5.0 kcal/mol) against human glucosidase (2QMJ). Rutin (-7.9 kcal/mol) also
exhibited excellent ADMET properties and was found to be more potent against alpha-amylase
(3IJ7) compared to glipizide (-7.8 kcal/mol) and biguanide (-4.3 kcal/mol). These studies reveal
the anti-diabetic activities of avocado peel to be linked to the presence of rutin, epigallocatechin
gallate and delphinidin-3-O-glucoside and therefore recommends these compounds for additional
in vivo animal studies and clinical trials to aid in the development and formulation of new antidiabetic drugs</jats:p>
title: Avocado Fruit Peel as a Source of Antidiabetic drugs: Evidence from Molecular Docking Studies and ADMET Profiling

items.abstract: <jats:p>Jhargram district in western West Bengal combines forested uplands, river corridors, pilgrimage and heritage sites, and community-based cultural resources that are relevant to nature-oriented tourism. This paper examines the distribution and functions of documented tourism assets, the principal considerations affecting their sustainable use, and practical priorities for destination management. A qualitative secondary-source case-study design was adopted, integrating district and state tourism records with peer-reviewed studies of Jhargram and wider research on community participation, environmental stewardship and rural tourism. The documentary assessment identifies complementary destination clusters centred on Jhargram town, Chilkigarh, Belpahari, and the Subarnarekha corridor. Official records also document a network of registered homestays and tourism-related facilities. Independently published geospatial research indicates substantial spatial variation in ecotourism suitability, while published stakeholder research draws attention to seasonality and unequal opportunities for participation. The paper proposes a site-sensitive planning framework that links visitor management, community decision-making, habitat protection, heritage interpretation and enterprise development. Its contribution lies in integrating verified destination information with independently published evidence and a transparent set of management implications, rather than estimating new visitor flows or economic impacts. The case suggests that appropriately scaled tourism development can complement local livelihoods when conservation responsibilities and benefit-sharing arrangements are treated as central planning requirements.</jats:p>
title: Tourism Resources, Development Constraints and Sustainable Planning in Jhargram District, West Bengal: A Secondary-Source Case Study

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Mendelian randomization (MR) studies use genetic variation to investigate possible causal relationships. Studies of adiposity, metabolic traits, and lung cancer often reuse the same genetic datasets, so agreement across publications may not represent independent confirmation. We evaluated the evidence while accounting for shared data sources and uncertainty in statistical synthesis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched through 24 May 2026. We assessed the comparability, data sources, and risk of bias of individual MR estimates before random-effects meta-analysis. We applied multiple-testing corrections, examined alternative statistical models, and repeated analyses after restricting estimates derived from shared genetic datasets.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Twenty-nine studies reported 163 eligible Mendelian randomization estimates. After screening and harmonization, 34 odds-ratio estimates contributed to 16 meta-analyses. In conventional random-effects analyses, associations of adult body mass index with overall lung cancer, lung squamous cell carcinoma, and small-cell lung carcinoma, and of waist circumference with overall lung cancer, remained statistically significant after both Holm and Bonferroni correction. However, none of the associations met either correction threshold under Hartung–Knapp or modified Hartung–Knapp inference. After GWAS-source restriction, 14 of the 16 relationships were represented by only one estimate; the remaining two relationships, adult body mass index and waist circumference with overall lung cancer, each retained two estimates. These source-restricted results varied across statistical models and were interpreted as exploratory because their frequentist P values were not adjusted for multiple testing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Although several associations met multiple-testing thresholds under conventional random-effects inference, they were not consistently supported across alternative inference methods. GWAS-source restriction also revealed limited relatively independent evidence. These findings warrant cautious interpretation and independent replication.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Systematic review registration</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PROSPERO CRD420261460092.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Adiposity and metabolic phenotypes in lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of mendelian randomization evidence with GWAS-source restriction
