<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To compare the real-world outcomes of a novel navigated panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) laser system with a modified wavelength of 577 nm and variable pulse duration with conventional argon laser PRP in retinal vasoproliferative disease.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Retrospective single-center cohort study of eyes treated with PRP for proliferative diabetic retinopathy (DR), central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) or other ischemic retinopathies. Argon laser PRP (2017–2020; argon laser cohort, ALC17/20) was compared with a navigated PRP laser system used at short pulse durations in two periods (navigated laser cohorts 2018–2020, NLC18/20, and 2022–2024, NLC22/24, after an in-house protocol change). The primary endpoint was retreatment-free survival; secondary endpoints were vitrectomy-free survival and laser parameters. Cox models were adjusted for age, indication, baseline disease severity and prior anti-VEGF treatment, with robust variance accounting for the inclusion of both eyes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A total of 497 eyes of 375 patients were included (ALC17/20: 160, NLC18/20: 206 and NLC22/24: 131 eyes). Compared to ALC17/20, navigated PRP used more pulses (median 1,542 in NLC18/20 and 2,043 in NLC22/24 vs 867 in ALC17/20), shorter pulses (30.0 ms in NLC18/20 and 23.8 ms in NLC22/24 vs 135.9 ms in ALC17/20) and less total energy (13,572 mJ in NLC18/20 and 15,645 mJ in NLC22/24 vs 28,403 mJ in ALC17/20, all
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001). Two-year retreatment-free survival was 72.2% in ALC17/20, 62.0% in NLC18/20 and 42.7% in NLC22/24. After adjustment for age, indication, baseline disease severity and prior anti-VEGF treatment, the risk of retreatment was not significantly increased in NLC18/20 (HR 1.37, 95% CI 0.91–2.05) compared to the ALC17/20 group, but remained increased in NLC22/24 (HR 2.38, 1.59–3.56), indicating a worse clinical outcome in this cohort; this finding was robust in landmark, time-split and weighted analyses. Vitrectomy rates did not differ (adjusted HR 1.28 in NLC18/20 and 1.16 in NLC22/24). Neovascularization of the disc or elsewhere, younger age and worse visual acuity were independently associated with retreatment rates, whereas pulse duration, total energy and number of sessions showed non-significant trends only.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Navigated PRP required more secondary interventions than argon laser PRP, partly because eyes with more active disease were more often selected for the new system; even after accounting for this, more retreatments were needed, indicating insufficient initial treatment. Vitrectomy rates did not differ. New laser systems should be accompanied by systematic evaluation of their efficacy and patient selection, and treatment protocols adapted accordingly.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Comparison of panretinal scatter photocoagulation in retinal vasoproliferative disease using argon laser vs navigated laser photocoagulation

items.abstract: <jats:p>Fluoride-salt-cooled high-temperature reactors and molten-salt reactors need compact, fouling-resistant primary-to-secondary heat exchangers that operate near atmospheric pressure at about 650 °C. Twisted tubes are a baffle-free, self-supporting candidate, but the available correlations cover narrow Reynolds number and modified Froude number windows and leave the shell side weakly characterized. Heat-transfer and friction correlations are developed for both sides of three stainless-steel twisted-tube heat exchangers, two of which differ only in twist pitch (101.6 and 76.2 mm) and one of which has a larger cross-section. Heat-transfer rates and pressure drops were measured in a counterflow water loop at 61 operating points, and the same geometries were modeled with steady Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) simulations. Because the shell-side pressure drop, 4.6 to 25.7 Pa, fell below the transducer resolution and the measurements give only the overall thermal resistance, the Nusselt numbers and friction factors were reduced from the simulations, which the measurements were then used to test. The simulated values follow power laws in within 2.3% and 1.8% over tube-side from 14,000 to 50,000 and shell-side from 1560 to 3070. Shortening the pitch from 101.6 to 76.2 mm raises the shell-side and tube-side Nusselt numbers by 15% and 6% at equal , at the cost of 72% and 19% higher friction factors, and the tube-side Nusselt numbers of the long tubes exceed the smooth-tube value by 30 to 55%. The measured convective resistance agrees with the prediction in the median for Tube 1 and differs from it by 31% and 34% for Tubes 2 and 3, which is attributed to the energy imbalance between the streams. The measured tube-side friction factors are a constant 0.50 of the simulated values for the long tubes, a factor attributed to the shape of the inner cross-section of the formed tubes, which was not measured, so the friction correlations rest on the simulations. On a Reynolds-number basis the correlations lie within the band of published twisted-tube data. The correlations apply to the two cross-sections tested and within the stated ranges.</jats:p>
title: Numerical and Experimental Investigations of Heat Transfer and Pressure Drop for Twisted-Tube Heat Exchangers

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    In 2021, I proposed that the diverse bioactive constituents associated with medicinal-leech salivary secretions could intersect with multiple molecular pathways involved in SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 pathogenesis. The original hypothesis focused particularly on protease-dependent viral entry, inflammatory proteases, coagulation and platelet activity, endothelial dysfunction, and other host processes potentially influenced by leech-derived molecules. Five years of research have substantially expanded understanding of SARS-CoV-2 protease biology, vascular injury, immunothrombosis, and host inflammatory responses. Continued characterization of medicinal and other blood-feeding leeches has likewise identified structurally and functionally diverse protease inhibitors, anticoagulant molecules, and complement-regulating proteins. Importantly, some of the molecular evidence incorporated into this reassessment predates or was published shortly before the original 2021 hypothesis, whereas other evidence emerged subsequently. This article therefore reassesses the 2021 hypothesis using independent SARS-CoV-2 literature together with molecular evidence concerning defined leech-derived compounds. Evidence supporting individual biochemical intersections is distinguished from mechanisms that remain theoretical, and species provenance is identified where relevant. Particular attention is given to Eglin C from
                    <jats:italic>Hirudo medicinalis</jats:italic>
                    , recombinant Cystatin-Hv derived from
                    <jats:italic>Haementeria vizottoi</jats:italic>
                    , and leech-derived molecules affecting complement and coagulation pathways. The accumulated evidence supports direct experimental investigation of selected leech-derived molecules against defined SARS-CoV-2-relevant host and inflammatory pathways but does not establish antiviral efficacy or clinical efficacy of hirudotherapy. Compound-specific dose-exposure relationships, cytotoxicity and safety, tissue accessibility, target-specific activity, and appropriate cellular and preclinical models require investigation before therapeutic conclusions can be drawn.
                  </jats:p>
title: Leech-derived bioactive molecules and SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis: revisiting a multi-target mechanistic hypothesis five years later

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In this work, highly reinforced self-cleaning nanocomposites based on low-density polyethylene (LDPE), polyvinyl butyral (PVB), and bismuth oxide (Bi
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    ) nanoparticles were successfully fabricated using electron-beam (EB) irradiation. LDPE/PVB blends with varying PVB contents were prepared to improve matrix compatibility. Among the investigated compositions, the LDPE/PVB (95/5 wt%) blend exhibited the optimum properties and was subsequently reinforced with 3 parts per hundred resin (phr) Bi
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    nanoparticles to fabricate LDPE/PVB/Bi
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    nanocomposites. The LDPE/PVB (95/5 wt%) composition showed optimum performance. Reinforcement with 3 parts per hundred resin (phr) Bi
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    nanoparticles to fabricate LDPE/PVB/Bi
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    nanocomposites using a Brabender-like mixing apparatus and subsequent exposure to EB irradiation at different doses (10–150 kGy). Gel fraction and crosslink density calculations confirmed that EB irradiation up to 100 kGy provides the optimum dose, as radiation-induced crosslinking strengthens the polymer network and results in pronounced improvements in mechanical strength, thermal stability, and interfacial interaction. Comprehensive characterizations were performed using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and contact angle measurements. The results confirmed homogeneous Bi
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    nanoparticle dispersion, enhanced structural integrity, and improved surface properties. The synergistic effect of PVB/Bi
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    incorporation into LDPE and EB irradiation markedly increased hydrophobicity, raising the water contact angle from 93° (neat LDPE) to 142° (irradiated nanocomposite). Furthermore, photocatalytic self-cleaning efficiency was significantly enhanced, achieving 94% methylene blue degradation under UV irradiation, compared to only 16% for neat LDPE. The kinetic analysis confirmed that the pseudo-first-order model provided superior correlation (R² = 0.985–0.998), establishing photocatalysis as the dominant degradation pathway. Overall, the developed LDPE/PVB/Bi
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    nanocomposites exhibited superior mechanical strength, thermal stability, hydrophobicity, and self-cleaning performance, demonstrating their potential for advanced packaging, environmental remediation, and outdoor engineering applications requiring durable multifunctional polymeric materials.
                  </jats:p>
title: Highly reinforced self-cleaning low-density polyethylene/poly(vinyl butyral)/bismuth oxide nanocomposites fabricated by electron beam irradiation

<jats:title>SUMMARY</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The global increase in the incidence of invasive fungal diseases and concurrent rise of antifungal resistance is a growing public health concern. In addition, persistent challenges in the development of novel antifungal agents underscore the need to identify alternative therapeutic targets. To meet these challenges of global concern, polyamine synthesis/transport inhibitors may potentially be used as therapeutic agents against mycoses. Polyamines play essential roles in fungal growth, stress responses, and virulence, rendering their metabolic pathways attractive candidates for therapeutic intervention. A deeper understanding of the contribution of polyamine metabolism to fungal biology and pathogenicity is therefore critical to rationally translate polyamine-targeted approaches into clinical practice. This article reviews the theoretical basis and tested application of targeting polyamine metabolism as an antifungal strategy and provides perspectives into an as yet underexplored aspect of virulence among clinically relevant fungi.</jats:p>
title: Polyamine metabolism as a drug target in clinically relevant fungi

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Pervious concrete (PC) serves as a highly porous pavement material enabling water infiltration, stormwater runoff reduction, and groundwater recharge. PC properties are often governed by factors such as aggregate shape, size, and pore characteristics, cement content, water–cement ratio, and additives. Although machine learning (ML) has transformed the construction industry by predicting conventional concrete properties, studies on PC with additives remain limited. Thus, the major objective of this study was to assess the effectiveness of ML models and algorithms in predicting the target properties of PC mixtures, including compressive strength (CS), porosity, and permeability, based on random forest (RF), gradient boosting (GB), and artificial neural network (ANN) using a master database of 350 data points covering 78 mixtures. An independent 36-point external validation set was used to assess model generalizability. The input parameters used for developing the models included water-to-cement ratio, aggregate-to-cement (a/c) ratio, density, and additives such as silica fume and crumb rubber. Performance metrics indicated that RF and GB outperformed ANN during CS prediction, with test coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.79 and 0.80, and root mean square error of 2.04 and 1.97 MPa, respectively. Further, mixture-level out-of-fold R2 of 0.45 (RF) and 0.44 (GB) represented the unbiased estimates. All three models predicted porosity and permeability with good to excellent accuracy (R2 = 0.83–0.98). Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations-based feature importance analysis revealed that density dominated CS prediction, and the a/c ratio governed porosity and permeability, thereby corroborating the distinct physical mechanisms controlling the mechanical and hydraulic performance of PC. All three ML models predicted the target PC properties with very good to excellent accuracy; however, the RF model showed the narrowest expected difference range (d3s) for predicted PC properties. It is envisioned that the proposed algorithms in this study can be readily applied in practice by entering component quantities in the same format as the training dataset. Overall, this research study contributed to comprehending the PC properties better and will serve as the foundation for a computational and statistical framework in the future to facilitate a paradigm shift toward developing environmentally sustainable and resilient roadway infrastructure materials/systems.</jats:p>
title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Machine Learning Models in Predicting the Target Properties of Modified Pervious Concrete Mixtures

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Recurrent functional tongue restriction after previous lingual frenectomies presents a clinical challenge, particularly when earlier surgical records are unavailable.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Case presentation</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A 22-year-old woman reported two previous scalpel frenectomies followed by recurrent restriction of tongue mobility. Before reintervention, maximum mouth opening was 51 mm, whereas opening with the tongue tip touching the incisive papilla was 16 mm (31.37%). Management comprised surgical release with a 980-nm high-power diode laser, histopathological examination of the excised tissue, perioperative photobiomodulation (808 nm before surgery and 660 nm afterward), and postoperative orofacial myofunctional therapy. Histopathology showed collagen-rich tissue consistent with fibrosis but could not establish its cause. Tongue-to-papilla opening increased to 29 mm immediately after surgery and measured 27 mm at eight months, an 11-mm improvement relative to baseline. At approximately 23 months, clinical examination showed a healed surgical site without clinically evident anterior frenulum reattachment; the patient reported satisfactory oral function without perceived recurrent tongue restriction. No standardized quantitative tongue-mobility measurement was obtained at this later visit.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This case documents favorable clinical and patient-reported findings after a multimodal reintervention. The individual contributions of laser surgery, photobiomodulation, and myofunctional therapy cannot be determined from a single case.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: High-power diode laser-assisted reintervention for recurrent fibrotic ankyloglossia following two scalpel frenectomies: a case report with 23​-month follow-up

items.abstract: <jats:p>The burden of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) continues to rise, posing a serious threat to global health. Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), as the primary risk factor for atherosclerosis, has been a key target in ASCVD prevention and treatment. However, many patients, despite achieving target LDL-C levels following standardized treatment, still face significant residual cardiovascular risk, suggesting that lipid-lowering therapy alone cannot fully halt atherosclerosis progression. Abundant studies demonstrate that chronic low-grade inflammation is present throughout atherosclerosis, and anti-inflammatory therapy can independently reduce the risk of cardiovascular events, giving rise to the cholesterol-inflammation fusion hypothesis. Today, ASCVD management has undergone a fundamental shift, moving from lipid-lowering to a dual-target era of lipid-lowering and anti-inflammation. Statins combine lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory effects, with proven cardiovascular benefits; they remain the cornerstone of ASCVD management in the dual-target era. Atorvastatin exhibits several notable features: a titratable dosing strategy that spans all risk categories, robust LDL-C lowering, and substantial suppression of inflammatory mediators, including C-reactive protein, interleukin-6, and tumor necrosis factor-α. Its distinctive pentasubstituted pyrrole structure confers high lipophilicity, which may contribute to its lipid-lowering activity. In addition, its active metabolites exert not only lipid-modulating effects but also marked anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. Multiple large trials have shown that atorvastatin achieves concurrent control of lipids and inflammation, accompanied by reductions in cardiovascular events. Taken together, the available evidence supports the combined lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory effects of atorvastatin across diverse patient populations, making it a well-validated option for the management of ASCVD.</jats:p>
title: The role and status of atorvastatin in the cholesterol and inflammation dual-target era: a narrative review

items.abstract: <jats:p>Silicon is considered to be a promising anode material for the next generation of lithium-ion batteries due to its high theoretical specific capacity. However, it will produce significant volume changes during the lithium insertion and delithiation processes, which further cause problems such as particle cracking, repeated rupture and formation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and loss of electrical contact. Silicon/carbon (Si/C) composite materials provide an effective way to alleviate the above problems by combining the high capacity of silicon with the good electrical conductivity, mechanical support capability and interface stabilisation of carbon materials. This article reviews the structural design of Si/C composite anodes, focusing on three typical structures (carbon-coated, embedded and hollow/porous), and compares their roles and limitations in interface protection, electron transmission, mechanical buffering and volume expansion control. Further analysis revealed that there are trade-offs between different structures in terms of performance, energy density, preparation complexity and scaled application. The future development of Si/C anodes requires further optimisation of the Si/C ratio, interface bonding, pore structure and multiscale structural design, while taking into account high performance, low cost and scalable manufacturing.</jats:p>
title: Recent Progress in the Structural Design of Silicon/Carbon Composite Anodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries

items.abstract: <jats:p>Due to the development of electric cars, portable electronic devices, and energy storage, lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have experienced an increase in energy density demand. However, restrictions associated with the design of classical electrodes hinder the improvement of batteries' characteristics. The present review article examines three types of anode materials, namely, graphite, graphene, and silicon, as well as their distinct features. First, despite low cost and reliable cycling ability, the capacity of graphite is limited by 372 mAh g⁻¹. Second, high conductivity and lithium storage capacities are provided by graphene, but there is a possibility of aggregation of its sheets that can cause instability. Last but not least, silicon attracts special attention owing to its potential capacity of 3579 mAh g⁻¹. But the constant expansion of silicon makes it harmful for the structure of the electrode and solid electrolyte interphase. In order to resolve these issues, three modification approaches, i.e., structural engineering, composite with carbon materials, and modification of the interface, are proposed. Experimental data support positive outcomes related to the use of such modifications and improvement of the electrode capacity and performance. At last, the drawbacks of silicon-containing anodes, namely production difficulties, electrode swelling, and gap between the experiment and industrial practice, are discussed.</jats:p>
title: Challenges in Achieving High Energy Density in Lithium-Ion Batteries: Anode Materials and Silicon Modification Strategies

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Metamorphic (de)volatilization reactions play fundamental roles in many geodynamic processes and are frequently associated with propagating reaction fronts, yet the mechanisms controlling front propagation remain poorly constrained. Here, we derive new analytical solutions for fluid pressure-driven (de)volatilization reaction fronts in porous rocks. The solutions predict that reaction-zone width increases with the square root of time, a scaling that arises from mass conservation across the moving reaction front rather than from classical hydraulic pore-pressure diffusion. Front propagation is governed by an effective diffusivity that depends on both hydraulic and chemical parameters, including reaction-induced density changes. Unlike conventional hydraulic diffusivity, which neglects reaction-induced density variations and generally predicts much faster propagation, the effective diffusivity captures the retardation of reaction fronts caused by density changes, with larger reaction-induced density changes producing slower propagation. In addition to a single-front formulation, we derive an analytical solution for two simultaneously propagating, coupled reaction fronts. The fronts are dynamically linked through mass conservation, preventing independent propagation and causing the leading front to advance faster than the trailing front. Both the single- and two-front solutions closely match numerical simulations. Application of the two-front model to published gypsum dehydration experiments shows that accounting for pore-water to pore-vapor transitions yields more realistic permeability estimates than single-front models. Application to natural metamorphic reactions predicts permeabilities between 10
                    <jats:sup>−18</jats:sup>
                    and 10
                    <jats:sup>−24</jats:sup>
                     m
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    , consistent with independent experimental, geophysical, and geological estimates. By analogy, the analytical framework can also be extended to chemically controlled reaction fronts governed solely by chemical diffusion. The analytical solutions provide a quantitative framework for estimating the timescales of natural and experimental (de)volatilization processes involving propagating reaction fronts.
                  </jats:p>
title: Beyond hydraulic diffusion: reaction front propagation and timescales in metamorphic (de)volatilization processes

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Low-temperature operation imposes severe limitations on lithium-ion transport in battery electrolytes, yet the coupled effects of solvent composition and fluorinated additives in the cold-temperature regime remain insufficiently resolved. Here, we combine classical molecular dynamics (MD) and machine learning (ML) to investigate 1 M LiPF6 electrolytes containing ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), and EC/EMC (3:7), with 0–10 mol % fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), from 298 to 233 K. The coldest states are treated as simulated liquid-like trajectories rather than demonstrated stable liquids. MD simulations quantify Li+ self-diffusion, Nernst–Einstein (NE) and Green–Kubo (GK) conductivities and local coordination, while Gaussian-process surrogates model the NE and GK conductivities across composition and temperature. Cooling produces a pronounced transport penalty, particularly in EMC-containing electrolytes, whose GK conductivity decreases by more than 98% at 233 K, compared with 90–95% in EC-rich systems. Li+ self-diffusion activation energies are 0.49–0.54 eV for EMC-containing systems and 0.27–0.29 eV for EC-based systems. Within the EC family, 0–2 mol % FEC gives comparable cold-temperature transport, whereas 5–10 mol % FEC shows lower GK conductivity retention at the coldest simulated temperature (statistically resolved only at 10 mol %). The analyzed coordination channels remain solvent dominated, and FEC is depleted from the Li+ first solvation shell, acting indirectly on bulk transport. The Gaussian-process surrogates achieve composition-disjoint cross-validated RMSE values of 0.56 and 0.57 mS cm–1 for NE and GK conductivity. Within the simulated liquid-like trajectories, temperature and host-solvent composition dominate the bulk-transport response, with FEC acting as a secondary modifier.</jats:p>
title:
Low-Temperature
Transport in Li-Ion Battery EC/EMC/FEC
Electrolytes: Molecular Dynamics and Machine-Learning Modeling

items.abstract: <jats:p>Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is the most common systemic vasculitis in people older than 50 years. Glucocorticoids (GC) induce remission in almost every patient. More than 40% of patients relapse during tapering, however, and most develop GC-related adverse events. Research on the pathogenesis of GCA over the past decade has identified several pathways that can be targeted, among them dendritic cell maturation, Th1 and Th17 polarization of CD4+ T cells, interleukin-6 (IL-6) production by stromal and senescent cells, granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) signaling and vascular remodeling. GC suppress the Th17 response efficiently but have little effect on the interferon-γ-driven Th1 response, which may explain persistent vascular inflammation and relapses. Two GC-sparing agents are now approved. Tocilizumab remains the reference treatment, and recent studies have tested much shorter GC regimens in combination with it. The Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor upadacitinib was effective in SELECT-GCA, and the 2-year data showed that most patients flared after its withdrawal. Results with interleukin-17A (IL-17A) blockade are discordant. Secukinumab was effective in the phase 2 TitAIN trial and in relapsing polymyalgia rheumatica but missed its primary endpoint in the phase 3 GCAptAIN trial, while real-world data in refractory GCA are encouraging. Trials of IL-23, IL-1β and tumor necrosis factor inhibitors were negative. GM-CSF receptor and T-cell co-stimulation blockade showed promising results in phase 2 trials. With more drugs available, the main clinical problem has become choosing the right one for a given patient and deciding when to start it. This review links the treatment of GCA to its pathogenesis and proposes a treat-to-target approach built on baseline risk stratification, predefined GC milestones and a recently proposed definition of difficult-to-treat GCA.</jats:p>
title: Treatment of giant cell arteritis: from arterial wall immunology to a treat-to-target strategy

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Cancer susceptibility is usually framed in terms of adult exposures and somatic evolution, yet evidence from selected childhood and adult cancers raises a narrower question: whether susceptibility is partly shaped during development. Developmental Origins of Health and Disease and life-course frameworks identify sensitive periods, yet do not explicitly connect developmental changes to tissue-specific carcinogenesis. This review adopts a target-tissue perspective and organizes evidence across four domains: developmental shaping of tissue susceptibility, target-tissue developmental context, generational exposure routes, and persistence or life-course propagation toward carcinogenesis. The Developmental Cancer Susceptibility Triad is a structured evidence-appraisal framework for evaluating tissue-specific hypotheses about developmental contributions to cancer susceptibility. It assesses whether three elements are jointly specified and supported: the target tissue and developmental window, the developmental exposure profile, and a testable route of persistence or life-course propagation toward carcinogenesis. Human evidence is most direct for defined carcinogenic exposures during development, particularly ionizing radiation and diethylstilbestrol. Growth-related measures show reproducible associations but do not resolve the underlying exposure, tissue alteration, or life-course mediation. Selected childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia subtypes provide a bounded example of prenatal initiation followed by postnatal clonal selection, but this sequence cannot be generalized to adult solid tumors. By distinguishing directly supported, inferential, and untested links and by identifying alternative explanations, the Triad clarifies the evidence required to evaluate tissue-specific developmental hypotheses more rigorously.</jats:p>
title: Developmental contributions to cancer susceptibility: a target-tissue life-course framework

items.abstract: <jats:p>Lithium-ion batteries are widely employed in electric mobility and energy storage applications, where accurate state-of-charge (SoC) monitoring is essential for safe and efficient operation. This paper proposes a contactless and computationally lightweight measurement system based on eddy current (EC) testing. The relationship between SoC and pouch-cell dilation is exploited, where EC sensors are utilized to monitor thickness variations through resonant-frequency shifts while the cell is mechanically constrained to mimic battery-pack conditions. An extensive experimental campaign was conducted on two pouch cells, each monitored by two EC sensors, over repeated charge–discharge cycles at C-rates ranging from 0.2C to 2C. Three third-degree polynomial regression strategies were developed and evaluated through Monte Carlo validation. The results demonstrate that grouped models achieve estimation performance comparable to individual models across 0.5–2C, while unified models exhibit reduced accuracy at 0.2C during charging. Individual models achieve overall mean absolute errors of approximately 5–12% during charging and 3–5% during discharging. Additional statistical analyses assess model stability, measurement repeatability, and sensor sensitivity across different SoC regions. The contactless measurement principle and low computational complexity make the proposed approach promising for cell-level monitoring and integration into battery management systems.</jats:p>
title: Contactless State-of-Charge Estimation for Li-Ion Pouch Cells Based on Eddy Current Testing

items.abstract: <jats:p>Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) performed for cardiac indications can incidentally visualize adjacent lung regions. A 43-year-old man (95 kg, 187 cm; body mass index, 27.2 kg/m2), a former smoker without respiratory symptoms or evidence of infection, underwent surgical aortic valve replacement for severe bicuspid aortic stenosis. No preoperative chest computed tomography was available. After induction, transesophageal lung ultrasound demonstrated tissue-like echogenicity in the dependent left lung adjacent to the descending thoracic aorta. During assist-control/volume-control ventilation, tidal volume was 500 mL, respiratory rate 18/min, positive end-expiratory pressure 7 cm H2O, peak pressure 20 cm H2O, and plateau pressure 15 cm H2O. Oxygen saturation was 99% at an inspired oxygen fraction of 0.60, and hemodynamics were stable. A sustained inflation to 30 cm H2O for 6 s was delivered using the anesthesia machine and adjustable pressure-limiting valve. The tissue-like region disappeared and was replaced by aeration artifacts. The peri-induction timing, absence of an infectious syndrome, and rapid reversibility favored anesthesia-associated atelectasis, although transient airway malposition and other causes could not be definitively excluded. Persistence was not reassessed. Although previously described, this visual report may remind clinicians of this application when TEE is otherwise indicated.</jats:p>
title: Real-Time Transesophageal Lung Ultrasound Visualization of Regional Left Lung Reaeration During Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: The right mainstem bronchus (RMSB) is short and highly variable in length, making right-sided double-lumen tube and bronchial blocker placement technically demanding. Two-dimensional (2D) axial computed tomography (CT) may systematically overestimate bronchial length relative to three-dimensional (3D) multiplanar reconstruction (MPR) because the RMSB courses obliquely to the axial plane. This study compared 2D and 3D CT measurements of RMSB length referenced to the right upper lobe (RUL) bronchial orifice. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, paired 2D and 3D measurements of the superior and inferior RMSB distances were obtained from preoperative chest CT in patients undergoing thoracic surgery. Agreement was assessed using Bland–Altman analysis and the intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC(2,1)]; paired measurements were compared with two-sided paired-samples t tests. Results: A total of 697 patients (405 male, 292 female) were analyzed. 2D measurements were significantly longer than 3D measurements for both distances (all p < 0.001). Mean bias (2D − 3D) was 2.56 mm for the superior distance (95% limits of agreement −1.67 to 6.79 mm; ICC 0.743) and 2.74 mm for the inferior distance (95% limits of agreement −2.34 to 7.83 mm; ICC 0.714). The direction of bias was consistent across sex, age, and height subgroups. Conclusions: Compared with 3D MPR, 2D axial CT consistently yields longer RMSB length measurements, and limits of agreement between the two methods are too wide for them to be used interchangeably in individual patients. 3D MPR may therefore be the preferred modality for planning right-sided lung isolation, particularly when airway anatomy is challenging.</jats:p>
title: Comparative Evaluation of Two-Dimensional Axial and Three-Dimensional Multiplanar Reconstruction for Right Mainstem Bronchial Morphometry

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Insulin resistance (IR) is a key mechanism in the development of metabolic syndrome (MS). Early identification of metabolic dysfunction remains a clinical challenge. We aimed to evaluate IR and siMS scores in overweight and obese individuals, assess their correlation with metabolic parameters, and define metabolic phenotypes based on siMS score categories. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 460 overweight and obese individuals (BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2), aged 30–80 years. Patients were categorized into five groups based on siMS score values. Anthropometric, biochemical, and metabolic parameters were assessed. Insulin resistance and sensitivity were evaluated using HOMA-IR, Matsuda index, QUICKI, and triglyceride–glucose index (TyG index). MS was defined according to International Diabetes Federation harmonized criteria. Results: The siMS score showed strong positive correlations with BMI, WC, glucose levels, mean fasting insulin concentration, triglycerides, HOMA-IR and TyG index (p < 0.001), and inverse correlations with HDL, QUICKI and Matsuda index (p < 0.001). Significant correlation (p < 0.001) was found between siMS scores and FLI > 60 with prevalence from 15.2% to 95.9%, through siMS groups. The prevalence of MS increased from 10% to 97.5% across siMS groups. Patients with siMS scores between two and three already had IR, especially in groups with siMS scores 2.51–2.99 where insulin sensitivity here starts to decline along IR, and 63.7% of them had FLI > 60. They demonstrated significant metabolic dysfunction despite not fulfilling MS criteria. Conclusions: The siMS score is a valuable and practical tool for early detection of IR and metabolic dysfunction. It enables identification of individuals at risk before the onset of overt MS and may guide timely preventive interventions.</jats:p>
title: Clinical Utility of the siMS Score for the Identification of Early Metabolic Dysfunction and Insulin Resistance in Overweight and Obese Patients

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background and Objectives: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly investigated for clinical decision support; however, their ability to predict quantitative densitometric parameters from non-imaging clinical information remains uncertain. This study assessed the accuracy, agreement, and exploratory discriminatory performance of GPT-5.6 Sol-generated lumbar and total hip T- or Z-score estimates against QCT-derived reference measurements. Materials and Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included 450 adults who underwent QCT examinations. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were provided to GPT-5.6 Sol using standardized patient-specific prompts without disclosing reference QCT measurements. Lumbar volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) was assessed using the 3D Spine module, whereas proximal femoral measurements were obtained using the CTXA Hip module of QCT ProTM software. Each patient was evaluated once. Prediction performance was evaluated using Pearson’s correlation coefficient (r), mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), Bland–Altman analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results: The mean age was 62.02 ± 13.17 years, and 424 patients (94.2%) were women. GPT-5.6 Sol-generated scores showed modest correlations with measured values for the lumbar spine (r = 0.383) and total hip (r = 0.262). The corresponding MAE values were 1.256 and 0.941, and RMSE values were 1.550 and 1.266, respectively. Mean prediction bias was +0.339 for lumbar scores and −0.236 for total hip scores. For identifying CTXA-defined total hip osteoporosis (T-score ≤ −2.5), the area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.700 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.615–0.782), with 27.7% sensitivity and 90.2% specificity. Exploratory discrimination of lumbar vBMD < 80 mg/cm3 yielded an AUC of 0.682 (95% CI: 0.626–0.738), with 61.2% sensitivity and 72.8% specificity. In an exploratory comparison, five-fold cross-validated linear regression yielded lower prediction errors than GPT-5.6 Sol across both anatomical sites and score-type subgroups. Conclusions: GPT-5.6 Sol demonstrated modest discrimination but limited individual-level accuracy in estimating QCT-derived bone density scores from clinical and laboratory information. Substantial prediction errors and low sensitivity for identifying CTXA-defined total hip osteoporosis indicate that GPT-5.6 Sol-generated estimates cannot substitute for direct densitometric measurements. Further investigations incorporating standardized prompting, reproducibility assessment, and external validation are warranted.</jats:p>
title: Accuracy and Agreement of GPT-5.6 Sol-Generated Bone Density Estimates with Quantitative Computed Tomography Measurements: A Retrospective Study of 450 Adults

items.abstract: <jats:p>A 38-year-old HIV-negative woman developed intermittent fever and multiple soft-tissue masses. [18F]FDG PET/CT demonstrated extensive intramuscular and subcutaneous lesions, an intramuscular mass anterior to the left sternoclavicular joint, pulmonary lesions, and nodal uptake. The blood cryptococcal antigen was positive, and sequencing of an aspirate from a right latissimus dorsi abscess detected Cryptococcus neoformans. After antifungal therapy, fever resolved. Follow-up PET/CT showed an overall decrease in lesion burden, with smaller soft-tissue lesions and lower [18F]FDG uptake.</jats:p>
title: Rare Findings of [18F]FDG PET/CT in a Single Patient Without HIV with Disseminated Cryptococcosis

items.abstract: <jats:p>Ollier disease is a rare, non-hereditary skeletal disorder characterized by multiple, asymmetrically distributed enchondromas and an increased risk of secondary malignancies. A 30-year-old woman with Ollier disease diagnosed in childhood, a resected left frontal glioblastoma, not otherwise specified (NOS; CNS WHO grade 4), and a left hilar mass histologically diagnosed as chordoma underwent whole-body 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) to assess the extent of disease. CT showed multiple lytic intramedullary lesions with chondroid ring-and-arc matrix mineralization, endosteal scalloping and expansile remodeling in the scapulae, humeri, left ribs, left iliac bone, femur and tibia, without cortical destruction, periosteal reaction or soft-tissue component; these lesions showed low FDG uptake (maximum standardized uptake value [SUVmax] 1.1–1.8). The thoracic mass showed intense heterogeneous uptake (SUVmax 9.1). In the context of two malignancies, the skeletal lesions raised the possibility of bone metastases. Their interpretation as enchondromas was based on the combination of characteristic CT morphology, asymmetric distribution, the clinical history and the stability of the scapular, proximal humeral and rib lesions compared with a chest CT obtained six months earlier, rather than on FDG uptake alone, which cannot exclude low-grade chondrosarcoma. This case illustrates a diagnostic pitfall of 18F-FDG PET/CT in oncologic staging.</jats:p>
title: 18F-FDG PET/CT Pitfall: Ollier Disease Mimicking Disseminated Bone Metastases in a Patient with High-Grade Glioma and an Intrathoracic Chordoma

items.abstract: <jats:p>To develop a multifunctional system, novel hydrogel matrices based on poly(vinylpyrrolidone), carboxymethylcellulose, poly(ethylene glycol), and agar were crosslinked via 30 kGy electron beam (e-beam). The functionality of the hydrogels was achieved through physicochemical and structural characterization. Additionally, cumulative wet-mass loss in buffer media and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) loading capacity/release profiles were evaluated and investigated using mathematical models employed in the design of pharmaceutical formulations. At 30 kGy, gel fractions reached 98.25% for H1 and 94.72% for H2. The calculated crosslinking-to-chain-scission yield ratios were 16.66 for H1 and 2.27 for H2, indicating that crosslinking predominated in both formulations. The swelling degree and 5-FU loading depended on pH, reaching higher swelling at neutral pH (1380–1580%) than in basic media (980–1090%). Under ambient conditions, the hydrogels showed a relative wet-mass retention of approximately 46% after 8 h. Optimal 5-FU loading (~30% at 200 mg/L) occurred at pH 5–6, while sustained release at pH 7.4 reached ~47–54% within 30 h. 5-FU release kinetics were best described by Weibull for H1 at pH 5.0, while Peppas–Sahlin performed comparably to Weibull for H2 at pH 5.0, and to Makoid–Banakar for both hydrogels at pH 7.4 (R2 = 0.99). The experimental profiles showed an initial rapid release phase followed by slower release. The experimental results demonstrate that hydrogels obtained through e-beam crosslinking support the loading and release of 5-FU.</jats:p>
title: Radiation-Induced Synthesis of Crosslinker-Free Hydrogels via E-Beam: Structural Dynamics and Controlled Drug Delivery

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Weakly supervised histopathology image segmentation aims to reduce the need for pixel-level annotations during training. Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) enables instance prediction using image-level labels, but the quadratic complexity of self-attention limits attention-based MIL at pixel resolution. This study develops an MIL framework with linear-complexity attention for segmentation at the input-image pixel resolution. Methods: We propose RWKV-MIL, based on the Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) architecture, to extend MIL from patch-level to pixel-level instance prediction. A class token provides bag-level predictions through a classifier shared with the instance tokens. The proposed H-RWKV block introduces Hilbert-WKV attention, which combines bidirectional WKV attention with Hilbert-curve scanning to preserve spatial continuity between adjacent tokens in the sequence. Negative and positive instance losses jointly constrain instance representation learning using bag-level labels. We evaluated the framework on the Colon, WSSS4LUAD, and CAMELYON16 datasets and conducted ablation experiments. Results: Across three independent training runs, RWKV-MIL achieved positive-image F1-scores of 0.865±0.005, 0.813±0.003, and 0.803±0.007 on Colon, WSSS4LUAD, and CAMELYON16, respectively. Conclusions: RWKV-MIL supports weakly supervised segmentation of cropped histopathology images using image-level labels and linear-complexity attention. The component analyses support the evaluated design while leaving limitations in localization, evaluation coverage, and statistical precision.</jats:p>
title: RWKV-MIL: Efficient Weakly Supervised Histopathology Image Segmentation via Hilbert Curve-Based Linear Attention

                    -infused borate-based glasses’ optical and shielding properties. The absorption spectra reveal distinct electronic transitions of Er
                    <jats:sup>3+</jats:sup>
                    and Nd
                    <jats:sup>3+</jats:sup>
                    ions. As doping shifts from Er
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    to CeO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    , there is a 3.385 to 2.402 eV energy band gap narrowing (for indirect ones), indicating structural changes and raised non-bridging oxygen (NBO) content. Urbach energy decreases, suggesting reduced disorder, while refractive index, dielectric constant and molar refraction rise due to elevated NBO concentration. Reflection loss increases, optical transparency declines, and the metallization factor confirms the glasses’ insulating behavior. The reduction in optical electronegativity indicates an enhanced electron-donating capacity, along with an increase in polarizability. Moreover, the prepared glasses’ radiation shielding features were studied over the wide 0.015–15 MeV energy range. The glass sample doped with Er
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    shows superior effective atomic number and linear attenuation coefficient. The half-value layer confirms that Er
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    -infused glass provides the best shielding with minimal thickness. The results from this work emphasize doping’s influence on the features of optical and shielding, positioning Er
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    -enriched glass as a robust photonic and nuclear radiation protection application candidate.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Structured reporting is increasingly used to standardize the assessment of focal bone lesions, but the CT Bone Reporting and Data System (Bone-RADS) was designed for incidental lesions, and its behavior in lesions referred for biopsy is less well defined. We assessed how CT Bone-RADS categories relate to histopathological malignancy, how reproducible they are, how their performance depends on cancer history, and whether they relate to biopsy yield in lesions referred for CT-guided biopsy. Methods: In this single-center retrospective study, 80 consecutive adults who underwent CT-guided core biopsy of a focal bone lesion were analyzed. Two musculoskeletal radiologists independently assigned a CT Bone-RADS category (1–4) on the pre-biopsy CT; reader 1 was the primary reader. Histopathology was the reference standard. Results: Of 73 lesions with a definitive diagnosis, 33 (45%) were malignant; seven biopsies (9%) were non-diagnostic. The malignancy rate was 8–15% in categories 1–3 and 78% (95% CI 63–89) in category 4; the AUC was 0.85 (0.76–0.93), and the category 4 cut-off had a sensitivity of 88% and a specificity of 80% (75% and 80% when non-diagnostic biopsies were counted as malignant). Inter-reader agreement was near-perfect (weighted κ = 0.93). No category 1–3 lesion was malignant in patients without a known malignancy (0/24; 10 further lesions in this stratum had no definitive result), whereas 24 of 25 category 4 lesions were malignant in patients with one. Conclusions: In this biopsy-selected cohort, two musculoskeletal radiologists from one institution agreed closely on the CT Bone-RADS category, and malignancy was concentrated in category 4; the malignancy rates differed according to cancer history, largely as expected from the difference in pre-test probability, and these subgroup estimates are imprecise and descriptive. These findings do not support using the category alone to withhold biopsy.</jats:p>
title: Diagnostic Performance of CT Bone-RADS in a Cohort of CT-Guided Bone Biopsies

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Otoscopic image classification can support computer-aided analysis of ear conditions, but conventional Vision Transformers (ViTs) may be computationally inefficient because all image tokens are processed uniformly. This study aimed to reduce the number of active transformer tokens while retaining benchmark classification performance. Methods: We propose Saliency-Guided Polar Token Routing (SgPTR), which organizes dense visual features into radial–angular polar tokens, assigns token-wise saliency scores, and forwards only the Top-K selected tokens to the transformer encoder. SgPTR was evaluated on the Ear Imagery and Otoscopic Image datasets. To address duplicate and near-duplicate redundancy, the evaluation was repeated with a fully specified leakage-control protocol based on SHA-256 and 64-bit dHash clustering, followed by a matched 10-seed comparison against the true 48-token Polar baseline. Results: On the original Ear Imagery benchmark, SgPTR achieved 98.75% accuracy and 98.75% Macro-F1 using 12 active tokens, corresponding to a 75% reduction from the 48-token candidate representation. On the reproducibly cleaned Ear Imagery split (372 images), SgPTR with K=12 achieved 0.9118±0.0304 accuracy versus 0.9105±0.0339 for the 48-token Polar baseline, with a paired mean difference of +0.13 percentage points and a bootstrap 95% confidence interval of [−2.89,+3.42] percentage points. The Otoscopic Image Dataset remained near saturation and is therefore interpreted primarily as a ceiling-effect benchmark rather than evidence of diagnostic superiority. Conclusions: SgPTR is an efficiency-oriented token-routing framework that reduces the active sequence by 75% while retaining similar observed mean performance in the matched cleaned-data comparison; no claim of statistical equivalence, non-inferiority, or clinical generalizability is made.</jats:p>
title: Saliency-Guided Polar Token Routing for Efficient Otoscopic Image Classification

items.abstract: <jats:p>Epilepsy, being a complex neurological disorder, is considered to result from an imbalance between GABAergic inhibition and glutamatergic excitation, leading to recurrent seizures, oxidative stress, and hippocampal neurodegeneration. This study investigated the anticonvulsant efficacy of Karanjin (a lipophilic furanoflavonoid from Pongamia pinnata), its synergistic interactions with standard anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs), and its neuroprotective effects against oxidative damage and hippocampal cell death. Anticonvulsant activity of high-purity Karanjin (97.25% by HPLC) was evaluated in male Swiss albino mice using the Maximal Electroshock and Pentylenetetrazol models at oral doses of 25, 50, and 100 mg/kg. Synergy studies analyzed fixed-ratio co-administration arrays of Karanjin with standard AEDs, including Phenytoin, Carbamazepine, Phenobarbitone, and Sodium Valproate. A Flumazenil reversal assay to confirm GABAergic activity and brain biomarker assays (MDA, SOD, CAT, GABA) were used to assess post-seizure neuroprotection, alongside histopathological evaluation of hippocampal subfields. Karanjin significantly reduced the duration of Tonic Hindlimb Extension in the MES model (p < 0.001 at 100 mg/kg) and markedly delayed the onset latency of PTZ-induced clonic seizures (p < 0.001). It showed supra-additive synergy with standard AEDs (allowing lower AED doses) and positive GABAA receptor modulation (reversed by Flumazenil). Additionally, Karanjin elevated brain GABA, suppressed MDA, restored SOD and CAT levels (p < 0.01), and preserved neuronal architecture in the CA1, CA3, and Dentate Gyrus hippocampal zones. Karanjin exerts robust anticonvulsant efficacy mediated via GABAA receptor modulation, coupled with significant antioxidant shielding and structural neuroprotection within the hippocampus, presenting a viable multi-target natural candidate for epilepsy therapy.</jats:p>
title: GABAergic Modulation and Antioxidant Shielding by Karanjin from Pongamia pinnata: Mechanistic Insights into the Attenuation of SeizureInduced Hippocampal Damage

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Durable fluorine-free water-repellent textiles require simultaneous control over surface roughness, interfacial energy, and structural stability, yet reinforcing a rough interface often compromises the topography required for low liquid adhesion. Herein, alkali-activated poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) fabric was sequentially modified by immobilization of bifunctional boron nitride (BN), thermally initiated lauryl methacrylate (LMA) grafting, and controlled thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) reinforcement to construct a hierarchical interface, with the resulting fabric denoted as PET-BLT, where B, L, and T refer to BN, LMA, and TPU, respectively. BN established a micro/nanoscale roughness scaffold, LMA reduced the surface energy, and TPU improved interfacial continuity without fully masking the BN-derived topography. The optimized PET-BLT fabric exhibited a water contact angle of 145.6° and a low sliding angle of 12.3°, together with persistent water repellency under mechanical abrasion, water spray, hot-water impact, and liquid-nitrogen treatment. In addition to wetting regulation, the BN-containing interface enhanced thermal transport, increasing the thermal conductivity from 0.125 to 0.232 W m–1 K–1, and improved ultraviolet (UV) protection, with the ultraviolet protection factor increasing from 3.5 to 37.2. The resulting fabric therefore integrates low-adhesion water repellency, interfacial durability, thermal-transport enhancement, and UV shielding within a single fluorine-free architecture, highlighting its potential for outdoor protective and sportswear applications.</jats:p>
title:
Fluorine-Free Polyester Fabrics for Durable Water
Repellency, Enhanced Thermal Transport, and Ultraviolet Shielding

items.abstract: <jats:p>An experimental and numerical investigation was conducted on a beam-to-beam self-centring connection incorporating superelastic shape memory alloy (SMA) plates and steel disc springs, hereafter termed the SMA-plate connection (SPC). The cyclic behaviour of a gap-minimised SPC specimen was characterised experimentally and compared with previously published results for a different gapped configuration (SPC-G). The gap-minimised specimen exhibited a flag-shaped hysteretic response, small residual deformation, and moderate energy dissipation. By contrast, SPC-G exhibited a low-stiffness stage during early loading and final unloading. This stage increased the deformation required to engage the principal resisting mechanism and lowered the initial stiffness. However, the self-centring response was not markedly degraded. A refined three-dimensional finite element (FE) model was developed. Its accuracy was assessed by comparing its predictions with the connection-level test results. Additional FE parametric analyses were conducted to further investigate the influence of the initial connection gap on the connection response. The results showed that increasing the initial gap extended the reduced-stiffness stage and slightly decreased the ultimate moment capacity. A computationally efficient connector-beam-truss model was then established to reproduce the principal hysteretic features and the gap-closing mechanism. The simplified model was used to analyse three-storey prototype self-centring steel frames with and without connection gaps under 30 mainshock-aftershock sequences. For the prototype frame with the adopted uniform connection gap, the analyses indicated higher maximum interstorey drift (MID) responses than those of the frame without gaps. The additional MID amplification associated with aftershocks was nevertheless smaller in the gapped frame. However, these differences are descriptive, as no statistical significance tests were performed. Residual drifts remained small and comparable for both frames. No consistent increase in residual drift was observed under the mainshock–aftershock sequences. For the analysed prototype and selected ground-motion sequences, the adopted connection gaps had only a limited influence on the system-level residual-drift response.</jats:p>
title: Investigation of a Self-Centring Beam-to-Beam Connection and Its Structure-Level Seismic Response

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: We aimed to determine if the concept of a late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) granularity score can be used to help predict outcomes in patients presenting with heart failure of presumed non-ischaemic aetiology. The secondary aim was to discover the prevalence of unrecognised myocardial infarction (MI) within this cohort and assess its association with adverse events. Methods: We prospectively recruited patients who had been diagnosed with heart failure (left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <50%) and referred for cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) assessment. Patients with an established diagnosis of coronary artery disease or known structural or congenital heart disease were excluded. A previously published LGE granularity score was calculated for each patient. Results: A total of 737 patients were included. One hundred and forty (19%) were found to have ischaemic LGE and were defined as unrecognised MI. Over a median of 3.4 years of follow-up, patients with unrecognised MI exhibited a higher composite all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalisation (27.9%) than those with non-ischaemic heart failure (12.9%). Patients with unrecognised MI and a granularity score of greater than seven had the highest risk compared to those with non-ischaemic heart failure even after adjustment for age, sex and LVEF (adjusted hazard ratio 2.85 (1.61–5.05, p < 0.001). Conclusions: Heart failure patients with unrecognised MI and a higher LGE granularity score had the greatest risk of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalisation, independently of age, sex, and LVEF. These findings suggest that the LGE granularity score may improve long-term risk stratification and support individualised management in patients with heart failure.</jats:p>
title: Late Gadolinium Enhancement Granularity Score in Patients Presenting with Heart Failure and Unrecognised Myocardial Infarction

items.abstract: <jats:p>Objectives: To assess the diagnostic yield of copy number variation sequencing (CNV-seq) and trio-based whole exome sequencing (trio-WES) across fetal congenital heart disease (CHD) subtypes and compare genetic findings between isolated and non-isolated cases. Methods: This retrospective study included 543 fetuses with CHD diagnosed by prenatal ultrasound who underwent invasive prenatal testing between January 2022 and September 2025. All cases underwent CNV-seq; karyotype analysis was performed in 294 cases, and 168 CNV-seq–negative cases subsequently received trio-WES. Results: In this retrospective cohort of 543 CHD fetuses, clinically significant chromosomal abnormalities were detected in 61 cases (11.23%), including 36 numerical chromosomal abnormalities and 25 pathogenic CNVs. A total of 168 fetuses with negative CNV-seq results received trio-WES testing. Pathogenic/likely pathogenic SNV-indels were identified in 15 of these 168 cases (8.93%). Chromosomal diagnostic yields were highest in endocardial cushion defects (41.67%), followed by single ventricle (27.27%) and left-sided lesions (21.62%). Higher molecular diagnostic rates were observed in fetuses with left-sided lesions (27.78%), tumors (16.67%) and right-sided lesions (9.52%). Notably, all abnormalities identified in endocardial cushion defects were chromosomal in origin, predominantly aneuploidies. The positive rate of chromosomal anomalies was higher in non-isolated CHD (20.33%, 25/123) compared with isolated CHD (8.57%, 36/420, P<0.01). Conclusions: CNV-seq followed by trio-WES improves the diagnostic yield in fetal CHD. The marked variation across CHD subtypes supports systematic genetic evaluation, particularly in subtypes with a higher likelihood of genetic etiology.</jats:p>
title: Subtype–Specific Genetic Spectrum of Fetal Congenital Heart Disease: A Retrospective Prenatal Cohort Study

items.abstract: <jats:p>Precision ellipsometry (PREL) is an optical technique that has high sensitivity, sufficient to measure the thickness of molecular layers on a reflecting substrate due to the use of a polarization modulator. To measure the thickness and the refractive index independently and simultaneously, we assembled two-beam PREL. A beam splitter directs a part of the reflected light to one modulator, which measures an increment in the ellipsometric parameter Δ, and the other part to the other modulator, which measures an increment in the ellipsometric parameter Ψ, both to high precision. Then, from Δ and Ψ, using a single-layer model, the thickness and the refractive index can be obtained. We investigated the attachment of gelatin to tannin and chitosan to tannin and found counterintuitive features in the signal from chitosan: an apparent decrease in the signal upon injection and an increase upon rinsing. Through the analysis of two-beam ellipsometric data, including the extinction coefficient of the substrate and the refractive index of the solution in our model, we explained the peculiar features of chitosan and revealed a unified pattern of molecular attachment: both gelatin and chitosan gave an increment in thickness after injection. Then, after rinsing with water, the thickness decreases as loosely packed layers are removed, leaving a denser layer of molecules with a higher refractive index. Overall, these results show that PREL, especially in its two-beam setup, has high analytical potential.</jats:p>
title: Two-beam ellipsometry for molecular multilayer analysis

items.abstract: <jats:p>CRISPR-Cas12-based molecular diagnostics offer attomolar-level sensitivity and high specificity through trans-cleavage activity, presenting a potential, rapid, and affordable alternative for Point-of-Care Testing (POCT). However, operational challenges across the pre-analytical, analytical, and post-analytical phases continue to hinder the transition to routine clinical service. This narrative review aims to evaluate the challenges related to sample preparation, matrix effects, and quality control in CRISPR-Cas12 diagnostics while examining their implications for the practice of medical laboratory technology. A structured literature search was conducted across four major databases (PubMed, Scopus, DOAJ, and Google Scholar) for open-access publications from 2016–2026, following the SANRA guidelines and the PRISMA 2020 selection flow. The synthesis indicates that extraction-free and one-pot reaction protocols can reduce turnaround time to 30–60 minutes, alleviate the manual pipetting burden on medical laboratory technologists, and minimize the risk of aerosol contamination. Furthermore, interference from biological inhibitors in complex specimens—such as blood, sputum, and urine—can be mitigated by integrating microfluidic partitioning and electrochemical biosensors, without compromising the limit of detection. Testing reliability is further enhanced through the lyophilization of reagents (eliminating reliance on a cold chain), the inclusion of multiplexed internal controls, and the use of calibrated, smartphone-based digital readout systems. The successful clinical implementation of CRISPR-Cas12 diagnostics requires the standardization of a robust, end-to-end workflow suitable for primary healthcare facilities, rather than relying solely on superior analytical performance within a laboratory setting.</jats:p>
title: Challenges in Sample Preparation, Matrix Effects, and Quality Control in CRISPR-Cas12 Diagnostics: Implications for Medical Laboratory Technology

items.abstract: <jats:p>Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is an aggressive biliary tract malignancy typically diagnosed at an advanced stage, resulting in poor overall survival and limited curative surgical options. Unlike most solid tumors, GBC develops within a biologically unique, bile-exposed niche continuously influenced by bile acids, cholesterol, phospholipids, bilirubin derivatives, inflammatory mediators, microbial metabolites, and extracellular vesicles (EVs). Recent advances in genomics, proteogenomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and bile-derived biomarker discovery have transformed the understanding of GBC from a purely mutation-driven epithelial malignancy to a metabolically rewired and spatially organized tumor ecosystem. This ecosystem is governed by complex interactions involving epithelial plasticity, immunosuppressive stromal remodeling, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndoMT), neutrophil recruitment, tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) polarization, and dysregulated cellular energetics. Key molecular axes including PGM5-lactate-STAT3 signaling, SCD1-mediated lipid desaturation, oxLDL-OLR1 neutrophil invasion, GPX3-mediated redox regulation, MDK-LRP1 macrophage crosstalk, OLFM4-PD-L1 immune evasion, and AREG-CXCL5 neutrophil recruitment, present actionable diagnostic and therapeutic vulnerabilities. Furthermore, bile and serum metabolomics, optical bile spectroscopy, and biliary EV fingerprinting show promising but preliminary diagnostic potential for minimally invasive detection, pending prospective multicenter validation. This review synthesizes the multi-omics landscape of GBC, integrating metabolic mechanisms, microenvironmental crosstalk, non-invasive biofluid diagnostics, and rational precision therapies.</jats:p>
title: Integrative multi-omics of metabolic reprogramming in gallbladder cancer: mechanisms, tumor microenvironment interactions, diagnostics, and therapeutic opportunities

items.abstract: <jats:p>Cell-free nucleic acids (cfNAs) are increasingly expanding the scope of precision medicine from static molecular diagnostics to dynamic, minimally invasive therapeutic decisions. While traditional tissue-based tests remain crucial for treatment selection, they are limited by their invasiveness, sampling bias, and difficulty monitoring molecular changes over time. Liquid biopsy methods analyze circulating DNA and RNA to provide complementary genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic information. They can also reflect tissue injury, treatment response, and molecular evolution. Advances in molecular profiling, sequencing, bioinformatics, and machine learning have broadened the range of cfNA biomarkers available for predictive modeling. In cancer, cfNA applications now span genomic, epigenomic, fragmentomic, transcriptomic, and multimodal biomarkers. These can support therapy selection, response assessment, resistance detection, minimal residual disease evaluation, and recurrence monitoring. Several plasma-based tests are now FDA-approved or performed in CLIA-certified laboratories. Outside oncology, potential uses include donor-derived cfDNA for graft health and immunosuppression management, as well as cfNA biomarkers for autoimmune, cardiovascular, neurological, and metabolic diseases. Public pharmacogenomic and multi-omic data, combined with computational modeling, open new avenues for discovering new therapeutic-response markers that can serve as liquid biopsy tests. Future clinical adoption will hinge on analytical sensitivity, predictive accuracy, rapid results, prospective validation of clinical utility, cost-effectiveness and accessibility, and delivering actionable molecular information during treatment decisions. Emerging rapid, localized technologies, such as real-time nanopore sequencing, may enable more comprehensive cfNA analysis directly in hospital labs, though validation hurdles remain. This review covers the biological basis, technological advances, therapeutic uses, regulatory pathways, and future prospects of cfNA-based precision medicine. Overall, these advances highlight cfNAs as dynamic biomarkers that can support treatment selection and longitudinal therapeutic assessment across cancer and other diseases. Importantly, clinical implementation is uneven: selected plasma tumor genotyping assays have established treatment-selection indications, whereas many other cfNA biomarkers, including DNA methylation, fragmentomic, and RNA-based markers, remain exploratory or require prospective demonstration of clinical benefit.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>The paper presents data from an enzyme immunoassay of the prevalence of serological markers of such helminthiasis as anisakidosis (late IgG class immunoglobulins), clonorhosis (late IgG class immunoglobulins) and opisthorchiasis (IgM and IgG in total) in the indigenous population of Kyzyl, Republic of Tuva. A total of 524 people were examined. Of these, there were 382 women and 142 men. The frequency of anisakidosis markers in the sample was the highest, 7.06 %. Clonorhosis markers are in second place in terms of frequency, 4.39 %, and opisthorchiasis is in third place, 1.72 %. In all three cases, the frequencies of helminthiasis markers predominate in the sample of women compared with men. All examined individuals who have markers of helminthiasis are recommended to contact medical specialists to exclude or conﬁrm infestations and further treatment.</jats:p>
title: Enzyme immunoassay diagnostics of the prevalence of markers of anisakidosis, opisthorchiasis and clonorhosis in tuvinians of Kyzyl

items.abstract: <jats:p>Increasing attention has been paid to precast steel–concrete composite structures owing to their eco-friendliness, fast construction and reliable quality. Ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC), with low self-weight and outstanding mechanical performance, greatly optimises the performance of precast steel–concrete composite beams. In this paper, the authors propose a novel demountable precast steel–UHPC composite beam with bolt shear connectors designed for disassembly and systematically study its flexural performance and design methodology. Three full-scale specimens are tested to analyse failure modes, load–deflection responses, interfacial load–slip characteristics and strain distribution, revealing the structural cooperative working mechanism. A refined finite-element model is built and calibrated against test results to clarify the internal load transfer mechanism, and parametric analyses are conducted to quantify how key design variables affect flexural behaviour. Theoretical formulas for flexural capacity are derived and verified by way of experimental and numerical data. Combining the generalised strain energy density and the Mann–Kendall criterion, a method is put forward to identify the flexural characteristic values for deeper mechanical interpretation. This research offers solid theoretical and technical references for the engineering design and application of precast steel–UHPC composite structures.</jats:p>
title: Bending performance and design of a demountable precast steel–UHPC composite beam

items.abstract: <jats:p>A coherent transfer circuit can preserve a logical qubit in an ideal model without outperforming simpler hardware implementations. We derive an exact receiver–discarded factorization for a specified five-qubit circuit acting on one logical qubit in a fixed two-dimensional code space; the corrected two-qubit map removes cross-parity coherence. A single acquisition on ibm_phoenix covers all four two-component GHZ-type resource patterns and 16 resource–control sectors (1746 circuits, 4096 shots each). Physical-recovery state fidelities range from 0.9237 to 0.9422, below the direct-preparation (0.9777) and SWAP-reference (0.9738) fidelities observed in the same acquisition. All 16 pointwise physical-recovery phase intervals exclude the ideal phase (offsets 0.1072–0.2426 rad). Leakage-preserving CP-TNI reconstructions yield mean code-space survivals of 0.9397–0.9562 and survival-weighted identity overlaps of 0.9079–0.9305. Exploratory goodness-of-fit tests and selected receiver–discarded correlations reveal additional deviations, but their counting intervals are neither family-wise discoveries nor coverage-validated under substantial constraint-boundary activity. Six IBM jobs constitute one approximately two-minute acquisition window, not independent replications; the reference circuits also use different physical routes. Thus the data demonstrate neither device-level identity nor comparative hardware advantage. The contribution is a reproducible, small-block diagnostic methodology for testing an exact ideal fixed-code prediction and explicitly recording its limitations.</jats:p>
title: Ideal Fixed-Code Channel Equivalence and Single-Session Hardware Diagnostics of a Five-Qubit Coherent State-Transfer Circuit

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Robust, validated, subtype-specific MRI-based predictive models are needed to predict breast cancer treatment response accurately and in a timely manner. This study aims to validate such models using data collected from a large, multicenter I-SPY 2 trial to enable personalized neoadjuvant therapy and optimize individual patient outcomes. Methods: This study included 2117 patients enrolled between May 2010 and June 2022 in the I-SPY 2 trial. The full cohort was randomly divided into training and test sets in a 70/30 ratio. Subtype-specific MRI prediction models were developed using functional tumor volume (FTV) derived from the dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI acquired at baseline (T0), early treatment (T1), and inter-regimen (T2). The endpoint for prediction was pathologic complete response (pCR), assessed at surgery. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was used to evaluate the overall performance of the model, and sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were evaluated for the optimal cut point selected by the Youden Index. Our analysis was subtype-specific, with breast cancer subtypes defined by hormone receptor (HR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) statuses. Results: FTV variables included in the optimal models differed by subtype: FTV percent change at T1 was selected for HR−/HER2+ and HR+/HER2+ cancers, and FTV percent change at T2 for HR+/HER2− and HR−/HER2− (triple-negative) cancers. Performance was similar in the training and test cohorts. AUCs estimated in the test set were HR+/HER2−: 0.68 [95% confidence interval: 0.59, 0.77], HR+/HER2+: 0.71 [0.59, 0.82], HR−/HER2+: 0.65 [0.46, 0.84], HR−/HER2−: 0.74 [0.67, 0.81]. Optimal cut points selected for individual subtypes also resulted in similar sensitivities, specificities, PPVs, and NPVs. Conclusions: We developed and validated breast cancer subtype-specific MRI models to predict pCR using longitudinal FTV measurements before and during neoadjuvant therapy. Our findings indicate that the optimal MRI time point for prediction varies by cancer subtype, with early-treatment FTV change showing the greatest predictive value for HER2+ breast cancer, whereas inter-regimen FTV change shows the greatest predictive value for HR+/HER2− and TNBC.</jats:p>
title: MRI-Based Models for Personalizing Neoadjuvant Treatment in Breast Cancer: A Validation Study
